source.text: Καὶ εὐθὺς πρωῒ συμβούλιον ποιήσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον δήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήνεγκαν καὶ παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately early a council having made the chief priests with the elders and scribes and all the Council, having bound Jesus they led [him] away and handed [him] over to Pilate.

en.L: And immediately, early in the morning, the chief priests, having held a council with the elders and scribes and the whole Council, bound Jesus, led [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away, and handed [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] over to Pilate.
en.B: As soon as it was morning, the chief priests met with the elders, the scribes and the whole Council and reached a decision. They bound Jesus, led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} off, and handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to Pilate.
en.R: Very early in the morning, the leading priests met with the leaders of the people, the teachers of God's law, and the whole Jewish council. They made their plan. They tied Jesus up and led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away. Then they handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to Pilate, the Roman governor.

vi.L: Và ngay sáng sớm, các thầy tế lễ cả, sau khi họp bàn với các trưởng lão, các thầy thông giáo và cả hội đồng, trói Đức Giê-xu, giải [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] đi và nộp [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] cho Phi-lát.
vi.B: Vừa sáng ra, các thầy tế lễ cả đã họp với các trưởng lão, các thầy thông giáo và toàn thể Hội đồng Công luận, rồi đi đến quyết định. Họ trói Đức Giê-xu, giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi và nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho Phi-lát.
vi.R: Sáng sớm hôm ấy, các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu họp với các nhà lãnh đạo trong dân, các thầy dạy luật của Đức Chúa Trời và cả hội đồng tối cao của người Do Thái. Họ bàn định kế hoạch. Rồi họ trói Đức Giê-xu và giải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi. Họ nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho Phi-lát, quan tổng đốc La Mã.

ko.L: 그리고 곧 이른 아침에 대제사장들이 장로들과 율법학자들과 온 공의회와 함께 회의를 하고 나서, 예수를 결박하여 끌고 가서 빌라도에게 넘겨주었다.
ko.B: 날이 밝자마자 대제사장들은 장로들과 율법학자들과 온 공의회와 함께 모여 결정을 내렸다. 그리고 예수를 묶어 끌고 가서 빌라도에게 넘겨주었다.
ko.R: 아주 이른 아침에 대제사장들이 백성의 지도자들과 율법을 가르치는 선생들과 유대 최고 의회의 모든 의원들과 함께 모였다. 그들은 계획을 세웠다. 그리고 예수를 밧줄로 묶어서 끌고 갔다. 그다음에 예수를 로마 총독 빌라도에게 넘겨주었다.

es.L: Y en seguida, muy de mañana, los principales sacerdotes, habiendo deliberado con los ancianos y los escribas y todo el Consejo, ataron a Jesús, [lo] llevaron y [lo] entregaron a Pilato.
es.B: Al amanecer, los jefes de los sacerdotes se reunieron con los ancianos, los escribas y todo el Consejo, y tomaron una decisión. Ataron a Jesús, se lo llevaron y se lo entregaron a Pilato.
es.R: Muy temprano por la mañana, los jefes de los sacerdotes se reunieron con los líderes del pueblo, los maestros de la ley y todo el Consejo Supremo de los judíos. Hicieron su plan. Ataron a Jesús y se lo llevaron. Luego se lo entregaron a Pilato, el gobernador romano.

fr.L: Et aussitôt, de bon matin, les chefs des prêtres, ayant tenu conseil avec les anciens et les scribes et tout le Conseil, lièrent Jésus, [{{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}]emmenèrent et [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] livrèrent à Pilate.
fr.B: Dès le matin, les chefs des prêtres se réunirent avec les anciens, les scribes et tout le Conseil, et prirent leur décision. Ils lièrent Jésus, {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmenèrent et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livrèrent à Pilate.
fr.R: Très tôt le matin, les chefs des prêtres se sont réunis avec les anciens, les spécialistes de la Loi et tout le grand conseil juif. Ils ont décidé ce qu’ils allaient faire. Ils ont attaché Jésus et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont emmené. Puis ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont livré à Pilate, le gouverneur romain.

sw.L: Na mara moja asubuhi na mapema, wakuu wa makuhani, wakiwa wamefanya shauri pamoja na wazee na waandishi na Baraza Kuu lote, walimfunga Yesu, wakamchukua, wakamkabidhi kwa Pilato.
sw.B: Kulipopambazuka tu, wakuu wa makuhani walikutana na wazee, waandishi na Baraza Kuu lote, wakafikia uamuzi. Wakamfunga Yesu, wakampeleka, wakamkabidhi kwa Pilato.
sw.R: Asubuhi na mapema sana, viongozi wa makuhani walikutana na wazee wa watu, walimu wa Sheria na Baraza Kuu lote la Wayahudi. Wakapanga mpango wao. Wakamfunga Yesu kamba, wakampeleka. Kisha wakamkabidhi kwa Pilato, mkuu wa mkoa wa Kirumi.

decisions.choice: having held a council: they met and reached a decision
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean to hold a meeting or to come to a decision, as in 3:6. After the night hearing (14:53-65), the leaders meet at dawn to agree on what to do with Jesus. Some manuscripts read "having prepared" a decision instead of "having made" one. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: chief priests, elders, scribes, the whole Council: the ruling Jewish council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: These groups together made up the Sanhedrin, the council that met under the high priest (8:31; 14:53, 55).

decisions.choice: Pilate: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea
decisions.reason: Pilate governed Judea for Rome from about AD 26 to 36. Under Roman rule the council could not carry out a death sentence on its own, so they brought Jesus to him.

decisions.choice: handed over: the word of Jesus' predictions
decisions.reason: Jesus had said the Son of Man would be handed over to the chief priests and that they would hand him over to the Gentiles (10:33). Now it happens.

decisions.choice: handed over
decisions.reason: All levels keep "handed over", the phrase used in the passion predictions (9:31; 10:33). Readable also calls the council "the whole Jewish council" and says who Pilate was.

decisions.choice: "các thầy tế lễ cả", "các trưởng lão", "các thầy thông giáo", "hội đồng" (L, B: "Hội đồng Công luận"); R "các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu", "các nhà lãnh đạo trong dân", "các thầy dạy luật", "hội đồng tối cao"
decisions.reason: The Protestant terms already used in John (11:47; 8:3) for the three groups of the ruling council; Readable says plainly who they were, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "nộp" for "handed over"
decisions.reason: The same verb as in John's passion story (John 18:35) and in Jesus' predictions; Mark repeats it through the chapter (15:10, 15:15), so Vietnamese keeps one verb for it.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서", "그분" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("말씀하신다", "불러 모은다", "입힌다", "끌고 나간다", "못 박는다"), through chapter 15
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (15:2, 15:16-17, 15:20-22, 15:24, 15:27); Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as the Korean of Mark 3-4 does.

decisions.choice: "대제사장들" at every level; "장로들", "율법학자들", "공의회" (L, B); "백성의 지도자들", "율법을 가르치는 선생들", "유대 최고 의회" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms of the Korean John (11:47) and of Mark 3:22; Readable says who these groups were, as the English Readable does. "대제사장들" is plain enough to keep at Readable, as the Korean John does.

decisions.choice: "넘겨주다" for paradidomi at every level, here and in 15:10 and 15:15
decisions.reason: The verb of Jesus' predictions that he would be handed over; one Korean word keeps the link, as in the Korean John's trial (18:30).

decisions.choice: los principales sacerdotes, los ancianos, los escribas, el Consejo (L); los jefes de los sacerdotes, los ancianos, los escribas, el Consejo (B); los jefes de los sacerdotes, los líderes del pueblo, los maestros de la ley, el Consejo Supremo de los judíos (R)
decisions.reason: The titles used in the Spanish of John (7:32, 8:3, 11:47, 19:6): Literal keeps the traditional titles; Balanced and Readable say who these men were (meaning decision m2). "Sumos sacerdotes" would suggest several high priests at once, and "escribas" today suggests copyists, so Readable says "maestros de la ley". The same words are used through this chapter.

decisions.choice: entregaron (every level)
decisions.reason: Mark uses one verb for handing Jesus over, the word of his predictions (meaning decision m4), and again in 15:10 and 15:15; every level keeps "entregar" for it so the repetition can be heard.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on stressed pronouns only (él, tú, ti, sí)
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish of John, the deity_pronoun setting covers the stressed pronouns for Christ. Clitics (lo, le, se) and possessives (su) are not spanned, so most of this chapter has no span where English has one.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping Mark's present tense ("ils convoquent" 15:16, "ils le crucifient" 15:24); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (15:1-47). The passé simple ("lièrent", "livrèrent") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where Mark tells a past event in the present, as the English Literal does, while Balanced and Readable use the past. Readable uses the passé composé ("ils ont attaché"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first.

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres (every level); les anciens (every level); les scribes, le Conseil (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi, le grand conseil juif (R); livrer (every level)
decisions.reason: The same French as in John: "les chefs des prêtres" at every level, "les anciens" at every level as in Mark 14:43 and 14:53, "les scribes" at Literal and Balanced and "les spécialistes de la Loi" at Readable (John 8:3), and the Council of meaning decision m2 named as a council rather than with the loanword "sanhédrin". "Livrer" is kept for this verb through the passion story, as in John 18-19, so that the reader can follow the chain from Jesus' predictions to Pilate (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani (L, B), viongozi wa makuhani (R); wazee; waandishi (L, B), walimu wa Sheria (R); Baraza Kuu
decisions.reason: The chief priests and scribes are named as in Swahili John (7:32; 8:3; 18:3): "wakuu wa makuhani" and "waandishi" at Literal and Balanced, and at Readable what they were, "viongozi wa makuhani" and "walimu wa Sheria". The ruling council (meaning decision) is "Baraza Kuu", capitalised as a body's name, so it is not taken for any meeting; a borrowed "Sanhedrini" would mean nothing to most readers. The same through chapters 15-16.

decisions.choice: kukabidhi for "hand over"; narrative past with -li- and -ka- at Balanced and Readable, historic present kept at Literal (15:16-27)
decisions.reason: "Kukabidhi" is the verb Swahili John uses for handing Jesus over to the authorities and to Pilate (18:30; 19:16), and it is kept here and in 15:10 and 15:15, so the link with Jesus' predictions (meaning decision) stays visible. Mark tells much of this chapter in the present ("they call together", "they clothe", "they crucify"); Literal keeps it, Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past. Swahili carries most pronouns inside the verb, where no capital can be shown, so the deity_pronoun setting appears only on free pronouns and possessives ("yake", "naye", "wangu"). This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

records.literal_gloss: And questioned him Pilate, You are the King of the Jews?

en.L: And Pilate questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the King of the Jews?"
en.B: Pilate questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the King of the Jews?"
en.R: Pilate asked Jesus, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the king of the Jewish people?"

vi.L: Và Phi-lát hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Anh là Vua của người Do Thái sao?"
vi.B: Phi-lát hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Vậy ra anh là Vua dân Do Thái à?"
vi.R: Phi-lát hỏi Đức Giê-xu: "Anh có phải là vua của dân Do Thái không?"

ko.L: 그리고 빌라도가 그분께 물었다. "네가 유대인의 왕이냐?"
ko.B: 빌라도가 예수께 물었다. "그러니까 네가 유대인의 왕이란 말이냐?"
ko.R: 빌라도가 예수께 물었다. "네가 유대인의 왕이냐?"

es.L: Y le preguntó Pilato: «¿Tú eres el Rey de los judíos?».
es.B: Pilato le preguntó: «¿Así que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres el Rey de los judíos?».
es.R: Pilato le preguntó a Jesús: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el Rey de los judíos?».

fr.L: Et Pilate {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogea : « Toi, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es le roi des Juifs ? »
fr.B: Pilate {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogea : « Alors, c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} le roi des Juifs ? »
fr.R: Pilate a demandé à Jésus : « Est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} es le roi des Juifs ? »

sw.L: Na Pilato akamwuliza, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Pilato akamhoji, "Kumbe {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.R: Pilato akamwuliza Yesu, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"

decisions.choice: the King of the Jews: a political charge
decisions.reason: To Pilate a man claiming to be king without Rome's approval was a rebel against Caesar. The council had asked whether Jesus was the Messiah (14:61); before Pilate the charge becomes kingship.

decisions.choice: You are: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: Pilate says "you" with emphasis: you, this prisoner, are the king?

decisions.choice: the king of the Jewish people
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words. Literal and Balanced keep the title as it stands on the charge in 15:26.

decisions.choice: Pilate to Jesus: "anh" for "you", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in John 18:33: a governor questioning a prisoner speaks down to him but not crudely. The English capitalisation setting has no counterpart, since Pilate's own word for Jesus is not the reverent "ngài".

decisions.choice: Pilate speaks to Jesus in the plain style (해라체: "네가 ... 왕이냐?"); "유대인의 왕" at every level
decisions.reason: As in the Korean John 18:33: the governor questions a prisoner. "유대인" already names the people, so Readable needs no other wording for the English Readable's "the Jewish people".

decisions.choice: el Rey de los judíos, with a capital, at every level; the stressed tú
decisions.reason: As in John 18-19 Spanish, the title is written with a capital through the chapter (15:9, 12, 18, 26), so the reader sees one charge (meaning decision m1). The Greek writes the pronoun out (meaning decision m2), and Spanish keeps it as the stressed "tú"; at the start of the question in Literal it needs no setting.

decisions.choice: Toi, tu es (L); c'est toi (B); le roi des Juifs, with lowercase "roi", at every level
decisions.reason: The stressed Greek pronoun (meaning decision m2) is shown by a stressed "toi" at Literal and "c'est toi" at Balanced. The title names the nation and is a political charge (meaning decision m1); French "le roi des Juifs" is plain enough for Readable, so French keeps it where the English Readable says "the Jewish people". French writes titles of office in lowercase, as in John 18:33.

decisions.choice: Wewe ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi, at every level
alternatives: Wewe ni mfalme wa watu wa Kiyahudi
decisions.reason: As in Swahili John 18:33: the title names the nation (meaning decision), so every level keeps "Mfalme wa Wayahudi" with the capital, where the English Readable says "the Jewish people". "Ndiwe" (you are the one) carries the stress on "you" (meaning decision).

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ λέγει· Σὺ λέγεις.

records.literal_gloss: And answering him he says, You say.

en.L: And answering him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "You say [so]."
en.B: He answered him, "You have said so."
en.R: Jesus answered, "Those are your words."

vi.L: Ngài trả lời ông và nói: "Ông nói [vậy]."
vi.B: Ngài đáp: "Chính ông đã nói vậy."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu trả lời: "Đó là lời của ông."

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그에게 대답하여 말씀하신다. "네가 말한다."
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "그것은 네가 한 말이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "그것은 네 입으로 한 말이다."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, respondiendo, le dice: «Tú [lo] dices».
es.B: Él le respondió: «Eso lo dices tú».
es.R: Jesús le contestó: «Esas son tus palabras».

fr.L: Et, lui répondant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Toi, tu [le] dis. »
fr.B: Il lui répondit : « C’est toi qui le dis. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « C’est toi qui le dis. »

sw.L: Naye, akimjibu, anasema, "Wewe unasema [hivyo]."
sw.B: Akamjibu, "Wewe umesema hivyo."
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Hayo ni maneno yako."

decisions.choice: he says: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: You say: a reply that accepts the title but leaves it in Pilate's mouth
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny it, but he does not take up Pilate's meaning either. Before the council he answered "I am" (14:62). Here his reply is guarded: the words are true, but the kind of king Pilate fears is not what Jesus is. Some take it as a simple yes.

decisions.choice: You: stressed, it is Pilate who says it
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, putting weight on Pilate as the speaker.

decisions.choice: You have said so (B); Those are your words (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the guarded form of the answer and do not turn it into a plain yes.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at L by leaving out "đã" ("nói"), here and through the chapter (15:16-27; 16:2-6)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs do not change for tense. Literal shows Mark's present-tense storytelling by leaving out the past marker; Balanced and Readable tell the story as past where Vietnamese needs it.

decisions.choice: Jesus to Pilate: "ông"
decisions.reason: As in John 18:34: Jesus addresses the governor as "ông", courteous without deference.

decisions.choice: "네가 말한다" (L); "그것은 네가 한 말이다" (B); "그것은 네 입으로 한 말이다" (R)
decisions.reason: The stressed "you" leaves the title in Pilate's mouth without denying it (meaning decision); Korean says that by putting "네가" in front. Jesus answers Pilate in 해라체, as in the Korean John 18:37.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice); pretérito at Balanced and Readable (respondió, contestó)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells his story in the present tense (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as Spanish stories are told. This applies to every such verb in the chapter (15:16, 17, 20, 21, 22, 24, 27).

decisions.choice: Eso lo dices tú (B); Esas son tus palabras (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "tú" last, where Spanish puts stress, so the reply accepts the title but leaves it in Pilate's mouth (meaning decisions m2, m3). "Tú" is Pilate and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: Toi, tu [le] dis (L); C'est toi qui le dis (B, R)
decisions.reason: French readers hear the familiar "Tu le dis" as a plain yes. The answer accepts the title but leaves it in Pilate's mouth, with the stress on "you" (meaning decisions m2 and m3); "c'est toi qui le dis" carries that stress in plain French, so Readable can use it too.

decisions.choice: Wewe unasema (L); Wewe umesema hivyo (B); Hayo ni maneno yako (R)
decisions.reason: The reply accepts the title but leaves it in Pilate's mouth (meaning decision), so no level says a plain "ndiyo" (yes). The free pronoun "wewe" gives the Greek stress on "you"; it is Pilate, so it takes no reader setting.

source.text: καὶ κατηγόρουν αὐτοῦ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς πολλά.

records.literal_gloss: And were accusing him the chief priests of many things.

en.L: And the chief priests were accusing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} of many things.
en.B: The chief priests kept bringing many charges against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The leading priests kept accusing Jesus of many things.

vi.L: Và các thầy tế lễ cả cứ tố cáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhiều điều.
vi.B: Các thầy tế lễ cả cứ đưa ra hết lời buộc tội này đến lời buộc tội khác chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu cứ tố cáo Đức Giê-xu nhiều điều.

ko.L: 그리고 대제사장들이 여러 가지로 그분을 고발하고 있었다.
ko.B: 대제사장들은 여러 가지 죄목을 들어 예수를 계속 고발했다.
ko.R: 대제사장들은 이런저런 일로 예수를 계속 고발했다.

es.L: Y los principales sacerdotes lo acusaban de muchas cosas.
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes presentaban muchas acusaciones contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes seguían acusando a Jesús de muchas cosas.

fr.L: Et les chefs des prêtres {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accusaient de beaucoup de choses.
fr.B: Les chefs des prêtres multipliaient les accusations contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Les chefs des prêtres n’arrêtaient pas d’accuser Jésus de toutes sortes de choses.

sw.L: Na wakuu wa makuhani walikuwa wakimshtaki kwa mambo mengi.
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani waliendelea kuleta mashtaka mengi dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Viongozi wa makuhani waliendelea kumshtaki Yesu kwa mambo mengi.

decisions.choice: were accusing: an ongoing action, charge after charge
decisions.reason: The tense pictures the accusations going on.

decisions.choice: many things: many charges, or with much insistence
decisions.reason: The word can mean many things or can mean strongly. Pilate's words in 15:4 ("how many things") show that many charges are meant.

decisions.choice: kept bringing many charges
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the ongoing tense.

decisions.choice: presentaban muchas acusaciones (B); seguían acusando (R)
decisions.reason: The imperfect and "seguir" show charge after charge (meaning decision m1); "muchas acusaciones" takes "many things" as many charges (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος πάλιν ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν λέγων· Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν;

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate again was questioning him, saying, Not you answer nothing?

en.L: And Pilate again questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not answer anything?
en.B: So Pilate put another question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} no answer at all?
en.R: So Pilate asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not going to answer?

vi.L: Phi-lát lại hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nói: "Anh không trả lời gì cả sao?
vi.B: Vì vậy Phi-lát hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lần nữa: "Anh không đáp lại gì hết sao?
vi.R: Vì vậy Phi-lát lại hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Anh không định trả lời sao?

ko.L: 그러자 빌라도가 다시 그분께 물으며 말했다. "아무것도 대답하지 않느냐?
ko.B: 빌라도가 다시 예수께 물었다. "아무 대답도 하지 않겠느냐?
ko.R: 빌라도가 예수께 다시 물었다. "왜 대답을 하지 않느냐?

es.L: Y Pilato otra vez le preguntaba, diciendo: «¿No respondes nada?
es.B: Entonces Pilato volvió a preguntarle: «¿No tienes nada que responder?
es.R: Por eso Pilato le preguntó otra vez: «¿No vas a responder?

fr.L: Et Pilate {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogeait de nouveau, en disant : « Ne réponds-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} rien ?
fr.B: Pilate {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interrogea encore : « Tu n’as donc rien à répondre ?
fr.R: Alors Pilate {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a questionné encore : « Tu ne vas rien répondre ?

sw.L: Na Pilato akamwuliza tena, akisema, "Hujibu chochote?
sw.B: Basi Pilato akamwuliza tena, "Huna jibu lolote?
sw.R: Basi Pilato akamwuliza tena, "Hutajibu kitu?

decisions.choice: not ... nothing: a double negative, expecting him to answer
alternatives: a statement that he did not answer
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer that Jesus surely will reply. The two negatives strengthen each other.

decisions.choice: was questioning: Pilate pressed him more than once
decisions.reason: The tense suggests repeated questioning.

decisions.choice: Have you no answer at all? (B); Are you not going to answer? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the question in natural English.

decisions.choice: ¿No respondes nada? (L); ¿No tienes nada que responder? (B); ¿No vas a responder? (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish, like Greek, uses two negatives together ("no ... nada") without cancelling them, so Literal keeps the form of the question, which expects an answer (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἴδε πόσα σου κατηγοροῦσιν.

records.literal_gloss: See how many things you they are accusing.

en.L: See how many things they are accusing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} of."
en.B: Look at all the charges they are bringing against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Listen to all the things they say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done!"

vi.L: Hãy xem họ tố cáo anh bao nhiêu điều."
vi.B: Kìa, họ đưa ra biết bao lời buộc tội chống lại anh!"
vi.R: Hãy nghe họ nói anh đã làm biết bao nhiêu điều kìa!"

ko.L: 보아라, 그들이 얼마나 많은 것으로 너를 고발하는지."
ko.B: 그들이 너를 얼마나 많은 죄목으로 고발하는지 보아라."
ko.R: 저 사람들이 네가 이런저런 일을 했다고 하지 않느냐! 들어 보아라!"

es.L: Mira de cuántas cosas te acusan».
es.B: Mira cuántas acusaciones presentan contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}».
es.R: ¡Escucha todo lo que dicen que has hecho!».

fr.L: Vois de combien de choses ils {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}accusent ! »
fr.B: Regarde toutes les accusations qu’ils portent contre {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ! »
fr.R: Écoute tout ce qu’ils disent que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait ! »

sw.L: Tazama ni mambo mangapi wanayokushtaki."
sw.B: Angalia mashtaka yote haya wanayoleta dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}!"
sw.R: Sikiliza mambo yote wanayosema kwamba umeyafanya!"

decisions.choice: See: look, pay attention
decisions.reason: The word draws attention, like "look".

decisions.choice: how many things: an exclamation
decisions.reason: Pilate is not asking the number. He points to the weight of the charges.

decisions.choice: Listen to
decisions.reason: The charges were spoken, so Readable says "listen".

decisions.choice: "들어 보아라" (R)
decisions.reason: The accusations are spoken, so Readable tells Jesus to listen to them, as the English Readable does; Literal and Balanced keep "보아라".

decisions.choice: Escucha (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the word calls attention (meaning decision m1); Readable says "listen", since the charges are spoken.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίθη, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν Πιλᾶτον.

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus no longer nothing answered, so as to amaze Pilate.

en.L: But Jesus no longer answered anything, so that Pilate was amazed.
en.B: But Jesus made no further reply at all, and Pilate was astonished.
en.R: But Jesus still did not say a word. Pilate was very surprised.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu không còn trả lời gì nữa, đến nỗi Phi-lát lấy làm lạ.
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu vẫn không đáp thêm lời nào, khiến Phi-lát rất ngạc nhiên.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu vẫn không nói một lời nào. Phi-lát rất ngạc nhiên.

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서는 더 이상 아무것도 대답하지 않으셨다. 그래서 빌라도가 이상히 여겼다.
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서는 더는 아무 대답도 하지 않으셨다. 빌라도는 몹시 놀랐다.
ko.R: 그래도 예수께서는 한마디도 하지 않으셨다. 빌라도는 무척 놀랐다.

es.L: Pero Jesús ya no respondió nada, de modo que Pilato estaba asombrado.
es.B: Pero Jesús no dio ninguna otra respuesta, y Pilato quedó asombrado.
es.R: Pero Jesús siguió sin decir ni una palabra. Pilato estaba muy sorprendido.

fr.L: Mais Jésus ne répondit plus rien, de sorte que Pilate était étonné.
fr.B: Mais Jésus ne répondit plus rien du tout, et Pilate en fut stupéfait.
fr.R: Mais Jésus n’a toujours rien dit. Pilate était très surpris.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu hakujibu tena chochote, hata Pilato akashangaa.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu hakujibu tena neno lolote, na Pilato akastaajabu.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu bado hakusema neno lolote. Pilato alishangaa sana.

decisions.choice: no longer answered anything: the silence of the suffering servant
alternatives: he did not hear the question
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:7 says the servant did not open his mouth, like a lamb led to the slaughter. Jesus had also kept silent before the high priest (14:61).

decisions.choice: no longer nothing: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: After his short answer in 15:2 he said nothing more at all.

decisions.choice: amazed: surprised, wondering
decisions.reason: Pilate was surprised that a man facing death would not defend himself.

decisions.choice: still did not say a word
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the double negative.

decisions.choice: siguió sin decir ni una palabra (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the strong double negative (meaning decision m2) in everyday words.

source.text: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν ἀπέλυεν αὐτοῖς ἕνα δέσμιον ὃν παρῃτοῦντο.

records.literal_gloss: Now at [the] feast he used to release to them one prisoner whom they requested.

en.L: Now at [the] feast he used to release to them one prisoner whom they requested.
en.B: At the festival it was his custom to set free for them one prisoner of their choosing.
en.R: Every year at the Passover festival, Pilate would set one prisoner free. The people could choose which one.

vi.L: Vào dịp lễ, ông thường tha cho họ một tù nhân mà họ xin.
vi.B: Vào mỗi kỳ lễ, ông có lệ tha cho họ một tù nhân do họ chọn.
vi.R: Hằng năm vào dịp Lễ Vượt Qua, Phi-lát thường thả một tù nhân. Dân chúng được chọn người sẽ được thả.

ko.L: 그런데 명절마다 그는 그들이 요청하는 죄수 하나를 그들에게 놓아주곤 했다.
ko.B: 명절이 되면 빌라도는 사람들이 원하는 죄수 하나를 풀어 주는 관례가 있었다.
ko.R: 해마다 유월절이 되면 빌라도는 죄수 한 명을 풀어 주었다. 어떤 죄수를 풀어 줄지는 사람들이 고를 수 있었다.

es.L: Y en [la] fiesta les soltaba un preso, el que pedían.
es.B: En cada fiesta, Pilato acostumbraba soltarles un preso, el que ellos eligieran.
es.R: Cada año, en la fiesta de la Pascua, Pilato dejaba libre a un preso. La gente podía escoger cuál.

fr.L: Or, à la fête, il leur relâchait un prisonnier qu’ils demandaient.
fr.B: À chaque fête, il avait coutume de leur libérer un prisonnier de leur choix.
fr.R: Chaque année, à la fête de la Pâque, Pilate libérait un prisonnier. Les gens pouvaient choisir lequel.

sw.L: Basi wakati wa sikukuu alikuwa akiwaachilia mfungwa mmoja waliyemwomba.
sw.B: Ilikuwa desturi yake, wakati wa sikukuu, kuwaachilia huru mfungwa mmoja waliyemchagua wenyewe.
sw.R: Kila mwaka wakati wa sikukuu ya Pasaka, Pilato alikuwa akimwachilia huru mfungwa mmoja. Watu waliweza kuchagua ni yupi.

decisions.choice: the feast: the Passover festival
decisions.reason: Mark has been telling of the Passover since 14:1. The custom belonged to this feast.

decisions.choice: used to release: a custom, done each year
decisions.reason: The tense describes what Pilate did regularly.

decisions.choice: the release of a prisoner: a custom known only from the Gospels
decisions.reason: No other ancient writer mentions this custom, but all four Gospels do (John 18:39). It was a favor to the people at their festival.

decisions.choice: Every year at the Passover festival
decisions.reason: Readable names the feast and makes the custom clear.

decisions.choice: "놓아주다" (L); "풀어 주다" (B, R) for apolyo, through 15:6-15
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean John 18:39 and 19:10; "석방하다" sounds legal and modern.

decisions.choice: Pilato, acostumbraba (B); Cada año, en la fiesta de la Pascua (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the imperfect describes a custom done each year (meaning decision m2), at the Passover festival (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable name Pilate, since the last person named was Jesus.

decisions.choice: relâcher (L); libérer (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in John 18:39: "relâcher" is the legal word for releasing a prisoner and keeps one verb through 15:6-15 at Literal; Balanced and Readable use the everyday "libérer". The French imperfect already says that this was a custom (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ἦν δὲ ὁ λεγόμενος Βαραββᾶς μετὰ τῶν στασιαστῶν δεδεμένος οἵτινες ἐν τῇ στάσει φόνον πεποιήκεισαν.

records.literal_gloss: Now there was the [one] called Barabbas with the rebels bound, who in the insurrection murder had committed.

en.L: Now there was the one called Barabbas, bound with the rebels who had committed murder in the insurrection.
en.B: A man named Barabbas was in prison along with the rebels who had killed people in the uprising.
en.R: A man named Barabbas was in prison at that time. He was with some men who had fought against the Romans. They had killed people during a riot.

vi.L: Lúc ấy có người gọi là Ba-ra-ba bị xiềng chung với những kẻ nổi loạn, là những kẻ đã phạm tội giết người trong cuộc nổi loạn.
vi.B: Có một người tên Ba-ra-ba đang bị giam cùng với những kẻ nổi loạn đã giết người trong cuộc bạo động.
vi.R: Lúc ấy có một người tên Ba-ra-ba đang ở trong tù. Người này bị giam chung với mấy kẻ đã nổi dậy chống lại người La Mã. Họ đã giết người trong một cuộc bạo loạn.

ko.L: 그런데 바라바라고 하는 사람이 반란 때에 살인을 저지른 반란자들과 함께 결박되어 있었다.
ko.B: 바라바라는 사람이 폭동 때 사람을 죽인 반란자들과 함께 감옥에 갇혀 있었다.
ko.R: 그때 바라바라는 사람이 감옥에 있었다. 그는 로마에 맞서 싸운 사람들과 함께 갇혀 있었다. 그들은 폭동을 일으켜 사람을 죽였다.

es.L: Y estaba el llamado Barrabás, preso con los rebeldes que en la revuelta habían cometido homicidio.
es.B: Un hombre llamado Barrabás estaba en la cárcel con los rebeldes que habían matado a gente en la revuelta.
es.R: En ese tiempo, un hombre llamado Barrabás estaba en la cárcel. Estaba con unos hombres que se habían levantado contra los romanos. Ellos habían matado a gente durante un motín.

fr.L: Or il y avait celui qu’on appelait Barabbas, enchaîné avec les insurgés qui avaient commis un meurtre pendant l’insurrection.
fr.B: Un homme appelé Barabbas était en prison avec les insurgés qui avaient tué des gens pendant l’insurrection.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, un homme appelé Barabbas était en prison. Il était avec des hommes qui s’étaient révoltés contre les Romains. Ils avaient tué des gens pendant une émeute.

sw.L: Basi alikuwapo yule aitwaye Baraba, amefungwa pamoja na waasi waliokuwa wamefanya mauaji katika uasi.
sw.B: Mtu mmoja aitwaye Baraba alikuwa gerezani pamoja na waasi waliokuwa wameua watu wakati wa maasi.
sw.R: Wakati huo mtu mmoja aitwaye Baraba alikuwa gerezani. Alikuwa pamoja na watu waliopigana dhidi ya Warumi. Walikuwa wameua watu wakati wa ghasia.

decisions.choice: Barabbas: an Aramaic name meaning son of the father
decisions.reason: Bar means son and abba means father. It was a family name, not a title.

decisions.choice: rebels, the insurrection: men who rose up against Roman rule
decisions.reason: The word means an uprising. The definite article points to an uprising Mark's readers knew of, though no other source names it.

decisions.choice: who had committed murder: the rebels did, and Barabbas was one of them
decisions.reason: The relative pronoun is plural. Barabbas is counted among the rebels who killed people. Luke 23:19 says he himself was in prison for murder.

decisions.choice: men who had fought against the Romans
decisions.reason: Readable says what the rebels had done. That the uprising was against Rome is clear from the setting, though Mark does not say it.

decisions.choice: "반란자들" (L, B) for stasiastes; "반란" (L), "폭동" (B, R) for stasis
decisions.reason: Men who rose up against Roman rule (meaning decision); "폭도" would make them a mere mob. "강도" is kept for lestes in 15:27.

decisions.choice: Barrabás; los rebeldes, la revuelta (L, B); unos hombres que se habían levantado contra los romanos, un motín (R)
decisions.reason: "Barrabás" is the usual Spanish form of the name (meaning decision m1). "Rebeldes" and "revuelta" are everyday words for men who rose against Roman rule (meaning decision m2); "sedición" is legal language. Readable says against whom, as the English does.

decisions.choice: les insurgés ... l'insurrection (L, B)
decisions.reason: The two Greek words share one root, and French "insurgés" and "insurrection" do too, so the link stays visible; both name a rising against Roman rule (meaning decision m2), which "émeute" alone would make sound like a street brawl.

decisions.choice: waasi; uasi (L), maasi (B), ghasia (R)
decisions.reason: The men had risen against Roman rule (meaning decision). "Waasi" are rebels against those in power and "uasi" or "maasi" a rising; "wahalifu" (criminals) would lose the political sense. Readable says whom they fought, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ ἀναβὰς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρξατο αἰτεῖσθαι καθὼς ἐποίει αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone up the crowd began to ask [him to do] as he was doing for them.

en.L: And the crowd went up and began to ask [him to do] as he usually did for them.
en.B: The crowd came up and began to ask Pilate to do for them what he always did.
en.R: A crowd came to Pilate. They asked him to set a prisoner free, as he always did.

vi.L: Và đám đông đi lên và bắt đầu xin [ông làm] như ông vẫn thường làm cho họ.
vi.B: Đám đông kéo đến và bắt đầu xin Phi-lát làm cho họ điều ông vẫn thường làm.
vi.R: Một đám đông kéo đến gặp Phi-lát. Họ xin ông thả một tù nhân, như ông vẫn thường làm.

ko.L: 그리고 무리가 올라가서, 그가 늘 그들에게 해 주던 대로 [해 달라고] 요구하기 시작했다.
ko.B: 무리가 빌라도에게 올라가서, 늘 해 주던 대로 해 달라고 요구하기 시작했다.
ko.R: 사람들이 빌라도에게 몰려왔다. 그리고 늘 하던 대로 죄수 한 명을 풀어 달라고 했다.

es.L: Y subiendo la multitud, comenzó a pedir [que hiciera] como solía hacer con ellos.
es.B: La multitud subió y comenzó a pedirle a Pilato que hiciera lo que siempre hacía por ellos.
es.R: Mucha gente llegó adonde estaba Pilato. Le pidieron que dejara libre a un preso, como hacía siempre.

fr.L: Et la foule, étant montée, commença à demander [qu’il fasse] comme il faisait pour eux.
fr.B: La foule monta et se mit à demander à Pilate de faire pour eux ce qu’il faisait toujours.
fr.R: Une foule est venue trouver Pilate. Les gens lui ont demandé de libérer un prisonnier, comme il le faisait toujours.

sw.L: Na umati ukapanda, ukaanza kuomba [awafanyie] kama alivyokuwa akiwafanyia.
sw.B: Umati wa watu ukaja, ukaanza kumwomba Pilato awafanyie kama alivyozoea kuwafanyia.
sw.R: Kundi la watu lilikuja kwa Pilato. Walimwomba amwachilie huru mfungwa mmoja, kama alivyofanya siku zote.

decisions.choice: having gone up: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a word that sounds alike and means "having shouted". The SBLGNT reads "having gone up", that is, the crowd came up to Pilate's residence, which stood on higher ground. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: as he was doing for them: as was his custom
decisions.reason: This points back to the custom of 15:6.

decisions.choice: the crowd: people who came for the release
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who they were. They had come to ask for the yearly release.

decisions.choice: Pilate (B); to set a prisoner free (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced names Pilate, and Readable says what they asked for.

decisions.choice: [해 달라고]
decisions.reason: Korean "요구하다" needs what is asked for; Literal brackets it, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: a Pilato (B); que dejara libre a un preso (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the request was for the customary release (meaning decision m2), so Balanced names Pilate and Readable says what they asked for.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς λέγων· Θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

records.literal_gloss: But Pilate answered them, saying, Do you want I should release to you the King of the Jews?

en.L: But Pilate answered them, saying, "Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?"
en.B: Pilate replied, "Shall I set free the King of the Jews for you? Is that what you want?"
en.R: Pilate asked them, "Do you want me to let the king of the Jewish people go free?"

vi.L: Nhưng Phi-lát trả lời họ, nói: "Các người muốn tôi tha cho các người Vua của người Do Thái không?"
vi.B: Phi-lát đáp: "Các người muốn tôi thả Vua dân Do Thái cho các người phải không?"
vi.R: Phi-lát hỏi họ: "Các người có muốn tôi thả vua của dân Do Thái không?"

ko.L: 빌라도가 그들에게 대답하여 말했다. "너희는 내가 유대인의 왕을 너희에게 놓아주기를 원하느냐?"
ko.B: 빌라도가 대답했다. "내가 너희에게 유대인의 왕을 풀어 주랴? 그것을 바라느냐?"
ko.R: 빌라도가 그들에게 물었다. "내가 이 유대인의 왕을 풀어 주기를 바라느냐?"

es.L: Pero Pilato les respondió, diciendo: «¿{{plural_you:Quieren|Queréis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} suelte al Rey de los judíos?».
es.B: Pilato les contestó: «¿{{plural_you:Les|Os}} suelto al Rey de los judíos? ¿Es eso lo que {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}}?».
es.R: Pilato les preguntó: «¿{{plural_you:Quieren|Queréis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} deje libre al Rey de los judíos?».

fr.L: Mais Pilate leur répondit, en disant : « Voulez-vous que je vous relâche le roi des Juifs ? »
fr.B: Pilate leur répondit : « Voulez-vous que je vous libère le roi des Juifs ? »
fr.R: Pilate leur a demandé : « Est-ce que vous voulez que je libère le roi des Juifs ? »

sw.L: Lakini Pilato akawajibu, akisema, "Mnataka niwaachilie Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Pilato akawajibu, "Je, niwaachilie huru Mfalme wa Wayahudi? Ndivyo mnavyotaka?"
sw.R: Pilato akawauliza, "Mnataka nimwachilie huru Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"

decisions.choice: answered: replied to their request
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, "answer" means to respond to what was said or done.

decisions.choice: the King of the Jews: Pilate uses the title with scorn
decisions.reason: Pilate takes up the charge (15:2). Spoken by him it mocks the leaders and the prisoner, but Mark's readers know it is truer than Pilate means.

decisions.choice: the king of the Jewish people
decisions.reason: As in 15:2.

decisions.choice: Pilate to the crowd: "tôi" for himself, "các người" for them
alternatives: "các ông" (as to the leaders in John 18:29)
decisions.reason: A Roman governor speaking to a crowd of subjects keeps his distance; "các người" is plain and a little cool, without the archaic "ngươi". He says "các ông" to the council members in John.

decisions.choice: Pilate speaks to the crowd in the plain style (해라체); the crowd shouts its demands in 하오체 ("십자가에 못 박으시오!", 15:13-14)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean John 18:39-40 and 19:6: the governor speaks down to the crowd, and the crowd's shouted demands to him take the older, firm 하오체.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Pilate speaks to the crowd, so every plural "you" takes the reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), here and throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: suelte (L); suelto (B); deje libre (R)
decisions.reason: "Soltar" is the word for releasing a prisoner, used again in 15:11 and 15:15; Readable says "dejar libre", the plainest form.

source.text: ἐγίνωσκεν γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παραδεδώκεισαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: He was knowing for that because of envy had handed over him the chief priests.

en.L: For he knew that it was because of envy that the chief priests had handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.
en.B: Pilate could see that envy was what had moved the chief priests to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to him.
en.R: Pilate knew that the leading priests had handed Jesus over to him because they were jealous of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Vì ông biết rằng vì lòng ghen tị mà các thầy tế lễ cả đã nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Phi-lát thấy rõ chính lòng ghen tị đã khiến các thầy tế lễ cả nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho ông.
vi.R: Phi-lát biết các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu nộp Đức Giê-xu cho ông vì họ ghen tị với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 대제사장들이 시기하여 그분을 넘겨주었다는 것을 그가 알고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 빌라도는 대제사장들이 시기심 때문에 예수를 자기에게 넘겨주었다는 것을 알고 있었다.
ko.R: 빌라도는 알고 있었다. 대제사장들이 예수를 시기해서 자기에게 넘겨준 것이었다.

es.L: Porque sabía que por envidia lo habían entregado los principales sacerdotes.
es.B: Pilato se daba cuenta de que los jefes de los sacerdotes se lo habían entregado por envidia.
es.R: Pilato sabía que los jefes de los sacerdotes le habían entregado a Jesús porque le tenían envidia.

fr.L: Car il savait que c’était par jalousie que les chefs des prêtres {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avaient livré.
fr.B: Pilate voyait bien que les chefs des prêtres {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avaient livré par jalousie.
fr.R: Pilate savait que les chefs des prêtres lui avaient livré Jésus parce qu’ils étaient jaloux de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana alijua kwamba wakuu wa makuhani walikuwa wamemkabidhi kwa sababu ya wivu.
sw.B: Pilato aliweza kuona kwamba wivu ndio uliowasukuma wakuu wa makuhani kumkabidhi kwake.
sw.R: Pilato alijua kwamba viongozi wa makuhani walimkabidhi Yesu kwake kwa sababu walikuwa na wivu juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: envy: jealousy of Jesus' standing with the people
alternatives: a just concern for the law
decisions.reason: The word means ill will at another's success. The leaders feared the crowds who listened to Jesus (11:18; 12:12).

decisions.choice: for: Mark explains why Pilate offered to release Jesus
decisions.reason: Pilate hoped the crowd would choose Jesus over the priests' wishes.

decisions.choice: had handed over: the same verb as in 15:1
decisions.reason: Mark keeps returning to the word of the passion predictions.

decisions.choice: to him
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "to him" so it is clear the priests handed Jesus to Pilate. The first "him" is Jesus, the second Pilate.

decisions.choice: se lo habían entregado (B); le habían entregado a Jesús (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable say that he was handed over to Pilate. "Entregar" is the verb of 15:1 (meaning decision m3), and "envidia" is jealousy of Jesus' standing (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: par jalousie (every level)
decisions.reason: French "envie" now usually means desire ("avoir envie de"), so "par envie" would be misread; "jalousie" names the resentment of Jesus' standing with the people (meaning decision m1).

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς ἀνέσεισαν τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μᾶλλον τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἀπολύσῃ αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd that rather Barabbas he should release to them.

en.L: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd [to ask] that he should release Barabbas to them instead.
en.B: But the chief priests worked up the crowd to have him free Barabbas for them instead.
en.R: But the leading priests got the crowd excited. They urged them to ask Pilate to free Barabbas instead of Jesus.

vi.L: Nhưng các thầy tế lễ cả xúi giục đám đông [xin] ông tha Ba-ra-ba cho họ thì hơn.
vi.B: Nhưng các thầy tế lễ cả kích động đám đông, để họ xin ông thả Ba-ra-ba cho họ thay vào đó.
vi.R: Nhưng các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu khích động đám đông. Họ xúi dân chúng xin Phi-lát thả Ba-ra-ba thay cho Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그러나 대제사장들은 무리를 선동하여, 그가 차라리 바라바를 그들에게 놓아주게 [하라고 요구하게] 했다.
ko.B: 그러나 대제사장들은 무리를 부추겨서, 오히려 바라바를 풀어 달라고 하게 했다.
ko.R: 그러나 대제사장들은 사람들을 부추겼다. 예수 대신 바라바를 풀어 달라고 빌라도에게 요구하게 했다.

es.L: Pero los principales sacerdotes incitaron a la multitud [a pedir] que más bien les soltara a Barrabás.
es.B: Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes agitaron a la multitud para que pidiera que les soltara más bien a Barrabás.
es.R: Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes alborotaron a la gente. Les dijeron que le pidieran a Pilato que soltara a Barrabás en lugar de Jesús.

fr.L: Mais les chefs des prêtres excitèrent la foule [à demander] qu’il leur relâche plutôt Barabbas.
fr.B: Mais les chefs des prêtres montèrent la foule pour qu’il leur libère plutôt Barabbas.
fr.R: Mais les chefs des prêtres ont excité la foule. Ils ont poussé les gens à demander à Pilate de libérer Barabbas à la place de Jésus.

sw.L: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani wakauchochea umati [uombe] kwamba afadhali awaachilie Baraba.
sw.B: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani waliuchochea umati, ili Pilato awaachilie Baraba badala yake.
sw.R: Lakini viongozi wa makuhani waliwachochea watu. Wakawahimiza wamwombe Pilato amwachilie huru Baraba badala ya Yesu.

decisions.choice: stirred up: shook up, incited
decisions.reason: The verb means to shake. It describes stirring people to action.

decisions.choice: that he should release Barabbas: the purpose of the priests' stirring
alternatives: what the crowd decided by itself
decisions.reason: The clause says what the priests aimed at.

decisions.choice: instead of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says whom Barabbas was chosen over.

decisions.choice: [하라고 요구하게]
decisions.reason: The purpose clause says what the crowd was to ask for; Korean needs the verb of asking, which Literal brackets as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: en lugar de Jesús (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says whom Barabbas was to be released instead of; the verbs "incitar", "agitar" and "alborotar" give the sense of stirring up (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τί οὖν θέλετε ποιήσω ὃν λέγετε τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate again answering was saying to them, What then do you want I should do [with him] whom you call the King of the Jews?

en.L: And Pilate again answered and said to them, "What then do you want me to do [with the one] whom you call the King of the Jews?"
en.B: Pilate spoke to them again. "Then what would you have me do with the man you call the King of the Jews?"
en.R: Pilate asked them again, "Then what should I do with this man? You call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the king of the Jews."

vi.L: Phi-lát lại trả lời và nói với họ: "Vậy các người muốn tôi làm gì với [người] mà các người gọi là Vua của người Do Thái?"
vi.B: Phi-lát lại nói với họ: "Thế thì các người muốn tôi xử thế nào với người mà các người gọi là Vua dân Do Thái?"
vi.R: Phi-lát lại hỏi họ: "Vậy tôi phải làm gì với người này? Các người gọi ông ta là vua của dân Do Thái."

ko.L: 빌라도가 다시 대답하여 그들에게 말했다. "그러면 너희가 유대인의 왕이라고 부르는 [그 사람을] 내가 어떻게 하기를 원하느냐?"
ko.B: 빌라도가 다시 그들에게 말했다. "그러면 너희가 유대인의 왕이라고 하는 이 사람은 내가 어떻게 하면 좋겠느냐?"
ko.R: 빌라도가 다시 물었다. "그러면 이 사람은 어떻게 할까? 너희는 이 사람을 유대인의 왕이라고 부르지 않느냐?"

es.L: Y Pilato, respondiendo otra vez, les decía: «¿Qué, pues, {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que haga con el que {{plural_you:llaman|llamáis}} el Rey de los judíos?».
es.B: Pilato volvió a hablarles: «Entonces, ¿qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que haga con el hombre al que {{plural_you:llaman|llamáis}} el Rey de los judíos?».
es.R: Pilato les preguntó otra vez: «Entonces, ¿qué hago con este hombre? {{plural_you:Ustedes lo llaman|Vosotros lo llamáis}} el Rey de los judíos».

fr.L: Et Pilate, répondant de nouveau, leur disait : « Que voulez-vous donc que je fasse [de celui] que vous appelez le roi des Juifs ? »
fr.B: Pilate reprit la parole : « Que voulez-vous donc que je fasse de l’homme que vous appelez le roi des Juifs ? »
fr.R: Pilate leur a demandé encore : « Alors, qu’est-ce que je dois faire de cet homme ? Vous {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}appelez le roi des Juifs. »

sw.L: Na Pilato akajibu tena, akawaambia, "Basi mnataka nimfanye nini yule mnayemwita Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Pilato akasema nao tena, "Basi mnataka nimfanye nini mtu huyu mnayemwita Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.R: Pilato akawauliza tena, "Basi nimfanye nini mtu huyu? Ninyi mnamwita Mfalme wa Wayahudi."

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do with the one whom you call: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: what shall I do with the King of the Jews (without "do you want" or "whom you call")
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "do you want" and some lack "whom you call". The SBLGNT keeps both. The sense is the same: Pilate puts the title on the crowd's lips. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: whom you call: Pilate distances himself from the title
decisions.reason: Pilate says it is their name for him, not his.

decisions.choice: then: since you want Barabbas
decisions.reason: The small word draws a conclusion from their request.

decisions.choice: Then what should I do with this man? You call him the king of the Jews.
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the question into two short sentences.

decisions.choice: "ông ta" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Pilate's own word for Jesus is "ông ta" (as in John 19:4), which has no reverent capital form, so the English span has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: [그 사람을]
decisions.reason: Korean "어떻게 하다" needs its object; the Greek has only "whom you call".

decisions.choice: ¿qué hago con este hombre? Ustedes lo llaman el Rey de los judíos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable splits the question; the stated "ustedes" keeps Pilate's distance from the title (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: yule mnayemwita, without a bracket
decisions.reason: The English Literal supplies "[with the one]". Swahili puts the object inside the verb ("nimfanye") and the relative inside "mnayemwita", and "yule" stands for the Greek relative pronoun, so nothing needs to be bracketed.

source.text: οἱ δὲ πάλιν ἔκραξαν· Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And again they cried out, Crucify him.

en.L: And they cried out again, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.B: They shouted back, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.R: The people shouted, "Nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross!"

vi.L: Họ lại la lên: "Đóng đinh ông ta!"
vi.B: Họ la lớn đáp lại: "Đóng đinh ông ta đi!"
vi.R: Dân chúng la lên: "Hãy đóng đinh ông ta trên cây thập tự!"

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 다시 소리 질렀다. "그를 십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.B: 그들이 되받아 소리쳤다. "십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.R: 사람들이 소리쳤다. "저 사람을 십자가에 못 박으시오!"

es.L: Y ellos gritaron otra vez: «¡Crucifícalo!».
es.B: Ellos volvieron a gritar: «¡Crucifícalo!».
es.R: La gente gritó: «¡Clávalo en una cruz!».

fr.L: Et eux crièrent de nouveau : « Crucifie-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! »
fr.B: Ils crièrent en retour : « Crucifie-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! »
fr.R: Les gens ont crié : « Cloue-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sur une croix ! »

sw.L: Nao wakapiga kelele tena, "Msulubishe!"
sw.B: Wakapiga kelele kumjibu, "Msulubishe!"
sw.R: Watu wakapiga kelele, "Mpigilie misumari msalabani!"

decisions.choice: again: in reply, once more
alternatives: a second time they said this
decisions.reason: The crowd has not yet called for crucifixion. The word here means back, in answer, or it looks back to their shouting for Barabbas.

decisions.choice: crucify: the Roman death for slaves and rebels
decisions.reason: The condemned man was fastened to a wooden cross and left to die. It was meant to shame and to warn.

decisions.choice: Nail him to a cross
decisions.reason: Readable explains what crucifixion was. Nails are attested for crucifixion, and the risen Jesus shows his hands (Luke 24:39; John 20:25).

decisions.choice: "ông ta" for Jesus in the crowd's cry, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As in John 19:6 and 19:15: the crowd would not use the reverent "ngài"; their own word has no capital form for the setting.

decisions.choice: "đóng đinh ... trên cây thập tự"
decisions.reason: "đóng đinh" already means to nail; Readable adds "on the cross" so a new reader sees what kind of death is meant, as the English Readable says "nail him to a cross".

decisions.choice: "십자가에 못 박다" for stauroo at every level, through chapter 15
decisions.reason: The word of the Korean John 19:6. It already says "nail to a cross", so Readable needs no other wording for the English Readable's "Nail him to a cross".

decisions.choice: Clávalo en una cruz (R); crucifícalo (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in English and in John 19:18 Spanish: Readable explains the Roman death (meaning decision m2) for readers who may not know "crucificar". The command is to Pilate, so it is singular and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: kusulubisha (L, B); kumpigilia misumari msalabani (R)
decisions.reason: "Kusulubisha" is the Swahili word for crucifying; Readable says what was done, "nail him to a cross", as the English Readable does and as Swahili John 19:18 does at Readable. The same through this chapter. Literal and Balanced add the object marker "-m-" (crucify him), which natural Swahili needs and which is part of the verb.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τί γὰρ ἐποίησεν κακόν;

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate was saying to them, What for did he do evil?

en.L: And Pilate said to them, "Why, what evil has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} done?"
en.B: Pilate asked them, "Why? What crime has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} committed?"
en.R: Pilate asked, "Why? What wrong has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} done?"

vi.L: Phi-lát nói với họ: "Vậy ông ta đã làm điều ác gì?"
vi.B: Phi-lát hỏi họ: "Tại sao? Ông ta đã phạm tội gì?"
vi.R: Phi-lát hỏi: "Tại sao? Ông ta đã làm điều gì sai?"

ko.L: 그러자 빌라도가 그들에게 말했다. "도대체 그가 무슨 악한 일을 했느냐?"
ko.B: 빌라도가 그들에게 물었다. "어째서냐? 그가 무슨 죄를 지었느냐?"
ko.R: 빌라도가 물었다. "왜? 그 사람이 무슨 나쁜 짓을 했느냐?"

es.L: Pero Pilato les decía: «Pues ¿qué mal ha hecho?».
es.B: Pilato les preguntó: «¿Por qué? ¿Qué delito ha cometido?».
es.R: Pilato les preguntó: «¿Por qué? ¿Qué cosa mala ha hecho?».

fr.L: Et Pilate leur disait : « Mais quel mal a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fait ? »
fr.B: Pilate leur demanda : « Pourquoi ? Quel crime a-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commis ? »
fr.R: Pilate a demandé : « Pourquoi ? Qu’est-ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait de mal ? »

sw.L: Na Pilato akawaambia, "Kwani amefanya ubaya gani?"
sw.B: Pilato akawauliza, "Kwa nini? Amefanya uhalifu gani?"
sw.R: Pilato akauliza, "Kwa nini? Amefanya kosa gani?"

decisions.choice: What for: why, with surprise
decisions.reason: The small word adds force to the question: why, what has he done?

decisions.choice: evil: wrongdoing, a crime
decisions.reason: Pilate asks what crime would deserve death.

decisions.choice: crime
decisions.reason: In a court the question is about a crime.

decisions.choice: Pilate speaks of Jesus as "그" / "그 사람" with no honorific
decisions.reason: Pilate is a Roman official speaking of a prisoner; the narrator still honours Jesus.

decisions.choice: delito (B)
decisions.reason: As in English: the evil asked about is a wrongdoing a court could punish (meaning decision m2).

source.text: οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραξαν· Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: But all the more they cried out, Crucify him.

en.L: But they cried out all the more, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.B: But they only shouted louder, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.R: But they shouted even louder, "Nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross!"

vi.L: Nhưng họ càng la lớn hơn: "Đóng đinh ông ta!"
vi.B: Nhưng họ lại càng la to hơn: "Đóng đinh ông ta đi!"
vi.R: Nhưng họ càng la to hơn nữa: "Hãy đóng đinh ông ta trên cây thập tự!"

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 더욱 크게 소리 질렀다. "그를 십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.B: 그러나 그들은 더 크게 소리를 질렀다. "십자가에 못 박으시오!"
ko.R: 그러나 사람들은 더 크게 소리쳤다. "저 사람을 십자가에 못 박으시오!"

es.L: Pero ellos gritaron aún más: «¡Crucifícalo!».
es.B: Pero ellos gritaron todavía más fuerte: «¡Crucifícalo!».
es.R: Pero ellos gritaron aún más fuerte: «¡Clávalo en una cruz!».

fr.L: Mais eux crièrent encore plus fort : « Crucifie-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! »
fr.B: Mais ils crièrent de plus belle : « Crucifie-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ! »
fr.R: Mais ils ont crié encore plus fort : « Cloue-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sur une croix ! »

sw.L: Lakini wao wakapiga kelele zaidi sana, "Msulubishe!"
sw.B: Lakini wao wakazidi kupiga kelele, "Msulubishe!"
sw.R: Lakini walipiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa zaidi, "Mpigilie misumari msalabani!"

decisions.choice: all the more: louder and harder
decisions.reason: The crowd does not answer Pilate's question. They only shout more.

decisions.choice: cried out: the same verb as in 15:13
decisions.reason: Mark repeats the verb and the shout.

decisions.choice: Nail him to a cross
decisions.reason: As in 15:13.

decisions.choice: Clávalo en una cruz (R)
decisions.reason: As in 15:13: the same cry, with the same words at each level (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος βουλόμενος τῷ ὄχλῳ τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιῆσαι ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν, καὶ παρέδωκεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας ἵνα σταυρωθῇ.

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate wanting the crowd the satisfactory to do released to them Barabbas, and handed over Jesus, having flogged [him], that he might be crucified.

en.L: And Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas to them, and having flogged Jesus, he handed [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] over to be crucified.
en.B: So Pilate, wishing to please the crowd, freed Barabbas for them. He had Jesus flogged and then handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over for crucifixion.
en.R: Pilate wanted to keep the crowd happy. So he set Barabbas free. He had Jesus beaten with whips. Then he handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to be killed on a cross.

vi.L: Phi-lát, vì muốn làm vừa lòng đám đông, tha Ba-ra-ba cho họ, và sau khi đánh roi Đức Giê-xu, ông nộp [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] để bị đóng đinh.
vi.B: Vậy Phi-lát, muốn chiều lòng đám đông, đã thả Ba-ra-ba cho họ. Ông cho lính đánh roi Đức Giê-xu, rồi nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để đem đi đóng đinh.
vi.R: Phi-lát muốn làm cho đám đông vui lòng. Vì vậy ông thả Ba-ra-ba. Ông cho lính lấy roi đánh Đức Giê-xu. Rồi ông nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho họ đem đi đóng đinh trên cây thập tự.

ko.L: 그래서 빌라도는 무리를 만족시키려고 바라바를 그들에게 놓아주고, 예수는 채찍질한 뒤에 십자가에 못 박히도록 넘겨주었다.
ko.B: 빌라도는 무리의 비위를 맞추려고 바라바를 풀어 주었다. 그리고 예수를 채찍질하게 한 뒤, 십자가에 못 박도록 넘겨주었다.
ko.R: 빌라도는 사람들을 만족시키고 싶었다. 그래서 바라바를 풀어 주었다. 그리고 병사들을 시켜 예수를 채찍으로 때리게 했다. 그다음에 예수를 십자가에 못 박도록 넘겨주었다.

es.L: Y Pilato, queriendo satisfacer a la multitud, les soltó a Barrabás, y entregó a Jesús, habiéndolo azotado, para que fuera crucificado.
es.B: Entonces Pilato, como quería complacer a la multitud, les soltó a Barrabás. Mandó azotar a Jesús y luego lo entregó para que lo crucificaran.
es.R: Pilato quería tener contenta a la gente. Así que dejó libre a Barrabás. Mandó que azotaran a Jesús con látigos. Después lo entregó para que lo clavaran en una cruz.

fr.L: Et Pilate, voulant contenter la foule, leur relâcha Barabbas, et livra Jésus, après [{{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}]avoir flagellé, pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit crucifié.
fr.B: Pilate, qui voulait satisfaire la foule, leur libéra donc Barabbas. Il fit flageller Jésus, puis {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livra pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit crucifié.
fr.R: Pilate voulait contenter la foule. Alors il a libéré Barabbas. Il a fait fouetter Jésus. Puis il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a livré pour qu’on {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} cloue sur une croix.

sw.L: Basi Pilato, akitaka kuuridhisha umati, aliwaachilia Baraba, na baada ya kumpiga Yesu mijeledi, akamkabidhi ili asulubiwe.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Pilato, akitaka kuuridhisha umati, aliwaachilia huru Baraba. Akaamuru Yesu apigwe mijeledi, kisha akamkabidhi ili asulubiwe.
sw.R: Pilato alitaka kuwafurahisha watu. Kwa hiyo alimwachilia huru Baraba. Akaagiza Yesu achapwe viboko. Kisha akamkabidhi ili apigiliwe misumari msalabani.

decisions.choice: to do the satisfactory to the crowd: to satisfy them
decisions.reason: The phrase is a Latin way of speaking put into Greek: to do enough for someone, to please them.

decisions.choice: flogged: scourged with a Roman whip
decisions.reason: The whip had pieces of bone or metal in its leather straps. Scourging came before crucifixion and could kill a man by itself.

decisions.choice: having flogged: Pilate's soldiers did it at his order
alternatives: Pilate did it with his own hands
decisions.reason: As often, the one who gives the order is said to do the act.

decisions.choice: handed over: the passion prediction fulfilled
decisions.reason: Jesus said the Gentiles would mock him, spit on him, flog him and kill him (10:34). Mark uses the same word for flogging.

decisions.choice: had Jesus flogged (B); had Jesus beaten with whips (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that Pilate gave the order. Readable says what flogging was.

decisions.choice: "채찍질하다" (L, B); "채찍으로 때리다" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean John 19:1; Balanced and Readable say that Pilate had it done ("-게 하다"), as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: mandó azotar (B); mandó que azotaran ... con látigos (R)
decisions.reason: As in English and John 19:1 Spanish: Pilate's soldiers did it at his order (meaning decision m3). "Azotar" is the everyday word for whipping (meaning decision m2). "Entregó" keeps the verb of 15:1 (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: [l']avoir flagellé (L); fit flageller (B); a fait fouetter (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 19:1: Literal keeps the Greek, which says that Pilate did what his soldiers did at his order (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable use "faire" with the infinitive. "Flageller" is the word for the Roman scourge (meaning decision m2); Readable says it in everyday words.

decisions.choice: kumpiga mijeledi (L); akaamuru apigwe mijeledi (B); akaagiza achapwe viboko (R)
decisions.reason: As Swahili John 19:1: the flogging was done by Pilate's soldiers at his order (meaning decision), so Balanced and Readable say he ordered it, as the English does. Readable uses "kuchapwa viboko", the everyday words for a whipping.

source.text: Οἱ δὲ στρατιῶται ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν ἔσω τῆς αὐλῆς, ὅ ἐστιν πραιτώριον, καὶ συγκαλοῦσιν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν.

records.literal_gloss: And the soldiers led away him inside the courtyard, which is [the] praetorium, and they call together all the cohort.

en.L: And the soldiers led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away inside the courtyard, that is, [the] praetorium, and they call together the whole cohort.
en.B: The soldiers took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} into the palace courtyard, that is, the governor's headquarters, and called the whole company of soldiers together.
en.R: The soldiers took Jesus into the courtyard of the governor's palace. They called all the other soldiers of their unit together.

vi.L: Các binh lính dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào bên trong sân, tức là dinh tổng đốc, và gọi tập hợp cả đội quân.
vi.B: Lính dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào sân trong của dinh, tức là dinh tổng đốc, rồi gọi cả đội lính đến.
vi.R: Những người lính đưa Đức Giê-xu vào sân của dinh quan tổng đốc. Họ gọi tất cả lính trong đơn vị đến.

ko.L: 그리고 병사들이 그분을 뜰 안, 곧 관정으로 끌고 갔다. 그리고 온 대대를 불러 모은다.
ko.B: 병사들은 예수를 총독 관저의 뜰 안으로 끌고 갔다. 그리고 부대 병사들을 모두 불러 모았다.
ko.R: 병사들은 예수를 총독이 머무는 관저의 안뜰로 끌고 갔다. 그리고 같은 부대의 다른 병사들을 모두 불러 모았다.

es.L: Y los soldados lo llevaron dentro del patio, es decir, [el] pretorio, y convocan a toda la cohorte.
es.B: Los soldados lo llevaron dentro del patio del palacio, es decir, a la residencia del gobernador, y reunieron a toda la compañía de soldados.
es.R: Los soldados llevaron a Jesús al patio del palacio del gobernador romano. Allí llamaron a todos los demás soldados de su compañía.

fr.L: Et les soldats {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmenèrent à l’intérieur de la cour, c’est-à-dire [le] prétoire, et ils convoquent toute la cohorte.
fr.B: Les soldats {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmenèrent dans la cour du palais, c’est-à-dire la résidence du gouverneur, et rassemblèrent toute la cohorte.
fr.R: Les soldats ont emmené Jésus dans la cour du palais du gouverneur romain. Ils ont appelé tous les autres soldats de leur unité.

sw.L: Na askari walimpeleka ndani ya ua, yaani, ikulu, nao wanakiita pamoja kikosi kizima.
sw.B: Askari walimpeleka ndani ya ua wa ikulu, yaani makao makuu ya mkuu wa mkoa, wakakiita pamoja kikosi chote cha askari.
sw.R: Askari walimpeleka Yesu ndani ya ua wa ikulu ya mkuu wa mkoa. Wakawaita pamoja askari wengine wote wa kikosi chao.

decisions.choice: courtyard: the court of the palace
decisions.reason: The word means an enclosed court and can stand for the palace around it, as in 14:54.

decisions.choice: praetorium: the governor's residence
decisions.reason: The Latin word was used for a commander's or governor's headquarters. In Jerusalem it was probably Herod's former palace, or else the Antonia fortress beside the temple.

decisions.choice: cohort: a unit of Roman soldiers, up to several hundred men
decisions.reason: A full cohort had about six hundred men. Mark likely means all the soldiers on duty there.

decisions.choice: they call together: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark tells the scene vividly in the present tense; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: the governor's headquarters; the whole company of soldiers (B); soldiers of their unit (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Latin terms. Balanced and Readable say what they were.

decisions.choice: "dinh tổng đốc" for the praetorium; "cả đội quân" (L), "cả đội lính" (B), "tất cả lính trong đơn vị" (R) for the cohort
decisions.reason: "dinh tổng đốc" as in John 18:28. A modern rank such as "tiểu đoàn" would put a precise size on a unit whose size here is uncertain; "đội quân" keeps it general.

decisions.choice: "관정" (L), "총독 관저" (B, R) for praitorion; "대대" (L), "부대" (B, R) for speira
decisions.reason: "관정" and "총독 관저" are the words of the Korean John 18:28. "대대" is the Korean military unit of several hundred men, close to a cohort; Balanced and Readable use the general word.

decisions.choice: el pretorio, la cohorte (L); la residencia del gobernador, la compañía de soldados (B); el palacio del gobernador romano, su compañía (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 18-19 Spanish, Literal keeps the Roman word "pretorio" and Balanced and Readable say what it was (meaning decision m2). "Cohorte" is the Roman unit (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable use "compañía", a plain word for a body of soldiers. Literal keeps Mark's present "convocan".

decisions.choice: le prétoire (L); la résidence du gouverneur (B); le palais du gouverneur romain (R); la cohorte (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in John 18:28, Literal keeps the Roman word and Balanced and Readable name the building (meaning decision m2). "Cohorte" is the French historical name of the Roman unit (meaning decision m3) and is understood by adult readers, so Balanced keeps it where the English Balanced says "company of soldiers"; Readable says "unit".

decisions.choice: ikulu (L), ikulu ... makao makuu ya mkuu wa mkoa (B, R); kikosi
decisions.reason: As in Swahili John 18:3 and 18:28: "ikulu" is the residence of a ruler, which is what the praetorium was (meaning decision), and Balanced and Readable say whose it was; a borrowed Latin word would mean nothing to most readers. "Kikosi" is a military unit, the sense of the cohort; "jeshi" would be a whole army.

source.text: καὶ ἐνδιδύσκουσιν αὐτὸν πορφύραν καὶ περιτιθέασιν αὐτῷ πλέξαντες ἀκάνθινον στέφανον·

records.literal_gloss: And they clothe him [in] purple, and they put on him having woven a thorny crown.

en.L: And they clothe {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [in] purple, and having woven a crown of thorns, they put [it] on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They put a purple robe on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, wove a crown out of thorny branches and put it on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.
en.R: They put a purple robe on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the color worn by kings. They twisted thorny branches into a crown and put it on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.

vi.L: Và họ mặc cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [áo] màu tía, rồi bện một vương miện bằng gai mà đội [nó] lên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Họ khoác cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng màu tía, bện một vương miện bằng gai và đội lên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Họ khoác cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} một áo choàng màu tía, là màu áo của vua chúa. Họ lấy những cành gai bện thành một vương miện và đội lên đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그분께 자주색 옷을 입히고, 가시로 관을 엮어 그분께 씌운다.
ko.B: 그들은 예수께 자주색 옷을 입히고, 가시나무로 관을 엮어 머리에 씌웠다.
ko.R: 그들은 예수께 자주색 옷을 입혔다. 자주색은 왕들이 입는 옷 색깔이었다. 그리고 가시 돋친 가지를 엮어서 왕관을 만들어 예수의 머리에 씌웠다.

es.L: Y lo visten de púrpura, y trenzando una corona de espinas, se [la] ponen.
es.B: Le pusieron un manto de color púrpura, trenzaron una corona de espinas y se la pusieron en la cabeza.
es.R: Le pusieron un manto de color púrpura, el color que usaban los reyes. Torcieron unas ramas con espinas para hacer una corona y se la pusieron en la cabeza.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} revêtent de pourpre, et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} mettent, l’ayant tressée, une couronne d’épines.
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} revêtirent d’un manteau pourpre, tressèrent une couronne avec des branches d’épines et la posèrent sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête.
fr.R: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont mis un manteau pourpre, la couleur des rois. Ils ont tressé des branches pleines d’épines pour en faire une couronne, et ils l’ont posée sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tête.

sw.L: Na wanamvika [vazi la] zambarau, na baada ya kusuka taji ya miiba, wanamvisha.
sw.B: Wakamvika vazi la zambarau, wakasuka taji kwa matawi ya miiba, wakaiweka juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.
sw.R: Wakamvika vazi la zambarau, rangi ya mavazi ya wafalme. Wakasokota matawi ya miiba kuwa taji, wakaiweka juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.

decisions.choice: purple: a royal color
decisions.reason: Purple dye was costly and was worn by kings. The soldiers may have used a faded red military cloak (Matthew 27:28) to look like a king's robe.

decisions.choice: a crown of thorns: a mock king's wreath
decisions.reason: Rulers wore wreaths. The soldiers made one of thorny branches to mock Jesus as king. It also caused him pain.

decisions.choice: they clothe, they put on: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As in 15:16, the sense is past.

decisions.choice: the color worn by kings
decisions.reason: Readable explains why purple was used.

decisions.choice: un manto de color púrpura (B, R); el color que usaban los reyes (R)
decisions.reason: The words of John 19:2 Spanish for the same scene. As in English: Balanced and Readable say it was a robe, and Readable says why the color mattered (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: un manteau pourpre (B, R); pourpre (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "purple", the royal color (meaning decision m1); French "robe" would suggest a dress, so Balanced and Readable name a cloak, as in John 19:2.

source.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀσπάζεσθαι αὐτόν· Χαῖρε, βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων·

records.literal_gloss: and they began to greet him, Hail, King of the Jews.

en.L: and they began to salute {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
en.B: Then they started saluting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Long live the King of the Jews!"
en.R: Then they began to bow and call out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Long live the king of the Jews!"

vi.L: và bắt đầu chào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Kính chào, Vua của người Do Thái!"
vi.B: Rồi họ bắt đầu chào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Kính chào Vua dân Do Thái!"
vi.R: Rồi họ bắt đầu cúi chào và hô lên với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Vua dân Do Thái vạn tuế!"

ko.L: 그리고 그분께 경례하기 시작했다. "유대인의 왕, 만세!"
ko.B: 그러고는 예수께 경례하며 외치기 시작했다. "유대인의 왕 만세!"
ko.R: 그다음에 예수 앞에서 절을 하며 외치기 시작했다. "유대인의 왕 만세!"

es.L: y comenzaron a saludarlo: «¡Salve, Rey de los judíos!».
es.B: Luego comenzaron a saludarlo: «¡Salve, Rey de los judíos!».
es.R: Luego empezaron a hacerle reverencias y a gritarle: «¡Viva el Rey de los judíos!».

fr.L: et ils se mirent à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} saluer : « Salut, roi des Juifs ! »
fr.B: Puis ils se mirent à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} saluer : « Salut à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, roi des Juifs ! »
fr.R: Puis ils ont commencé à s’incliner devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} en criant : « Vive le roi des Juifs ! »

sw.L: na wakaanza kumsalimu, "Salamu, Mfalme wa Wayahudi!"
sw.B: Kisha wakaanza kumsalimu, "Salamu, ee Mfalme wa Wayahudi!"
sw.R: Kisha wakaanza kumwinamia na kumwita, "Uishi milele, Mfalme wa Wayahudi!"

decisions.choice: Hail: the greeting given to an emperor
decisions.reason: Soldiers greeted the emperor with "Hail, Caesar". They mock Jesus with the same form.

decisions.choice: to salute: to greet with respect
decisions.reason: The verb means to greet. Here it is a mocking salute.

decisions.choice: Long live
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a cheer for a ruler that is still in use. Literal keeps the traditional "Hail".

decisions.choice: "Kính chào" (L, B), as in John 19:3; "vạn tuế" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the greeting as John's soldiers say it. Readable uses "vạn tuế", the cry with which subjects hailed an emperor, so a new reader hears the mockery of a royal salute, as the English "Long live" does.

decisions.choice: "만세" for chaire at every level; "경례하다" (L, B), "절을 하다" (R) for aspazomai
decisions.reason: "만세" is the Korean acclamation of a king or emperor, the word of the Korean John 19:3; the soldiers salute him as soldiers salute a ruler.

decisions.choice: ¡Salve! (L, B); ¡Viva! (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 19:3 Spanish: "salve" is the old word for hailing a ruler (meaning decision m1), still understood; Readable uses the cry with which people acclaim a king.

decisions.choice: Salut (L); Salut à toi (B); Vive (R)
decisions.reason: The same French as in John 19:3. The word is the greeting given to an emperor (meaning decision m1); bare "Salut" sounds casual in French, so Balanced makes it a formal greeting, and Readable uses the cry of acclaim.

decisions.choice: Salamu (L); Salamu, ee (B); Uishi milele (R)
decisions.reason: As in Swahili John 19:3: the soldiers use the greeting given to an emperor (meaning decision). "Salamu" is the plain greeting; Balanced adds the vocative "ee", used in solemn address to a king, so the mock homage is heard; Readable says "uishi milele" (long may you live), the cry for a king. "Shikamoo", the respectful greeting to an elder, would bring the wrong picture.

source.text: καὶ ἔτυπτον αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν καλάμῳ καὶ ἐνέπτυον αὐτῷ, καὶ τιθέντες τὰ γόνατα προσεκύνουν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And they were striking his head with a reed and were spitting on him, and bending the knees were bowing down to him.

en.L: And they kept striking {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head with a reed and spitting on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and bending [their] knees, they were bowing down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Again and again they hit {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the head with a stick, spat on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and went down on their knees to pay {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} homage.
en.R: They kept hitting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the head with a stick and spitting on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They got down on their knees in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were a king.

vi.L: Và họ cứ lấy cây sậy đánh vào đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, nhổ vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, rồi quỳ gối xuống lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Họ lấy gậy đánh vào đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hết lần này đến lần khác, nhổ vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, rồi quỳ xuống bái lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Họ cứ lấy gậy đánh vào đầu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nhổ vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ quỳ gối trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như thể {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là một vị vua.

ko.L: 그리고 갈대로 그분의 머리를 계속 때리고 그분께 침을 뱉고, 무릎을 꿇고 그분께 절하였다.
ko.B: 그들은 갈대 막대기로 예수의 머리를 거듭 때리고 침을 뱉었으며, 무릎을 꿇고 절을 했다.
ko.R: 그들은 막대기로 예수의 머리를 계속 때리고, 예수께 침을 뱉었다. 그리고 마치 왕에게 하듯이 예수 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 절을 했다.

es.L: Y le golpeaban la cabeza con una caña y le escupían, y doblando las rodillas, se postraban ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Una y otra vez le pegaban en la cabeza con una vara, le escupían y se ponían de rodillas para rendirle homenaje.
es.R: Le seguían pegando en la cabeza con una vara y escupiéndole. Se ponían de rodillas delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, como si fuera un rey.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} frappaient la tête avec un roseau et crachaient sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et, pliant les genoux, ils se prosternaient devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: À coups répétés, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} frappaient à la tête avec un bâton, crachaient sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et se mettaient à genoux pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendre hommage.
fr.R: Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} frappaient sans arrêt sur la tête avec un bâton et ils crachaient sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils se mettaient à genoux devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, comme s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était un roi.

sw.L: Na walikuwa wakimpiga kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} kwa mwanzi na kumtemea mate, na wakipiga magoti walikuwa wakimsujudia.
sw.B: Mara kwa mara walimpiga kichwani kwa fimbo, wakamtemea mate, wakapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kumsujudia.
sw.R: Waliendelea kumpiga kichwani kwa fimbo na kumtemea mate. Walipiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kana kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni mfalme.

decisions.choice: a reed: a stick or cane
