decisions.reason: The reed may have been given him as a mock scepter (Matthew 27:29) before they hit him with it.

decisions.choice: bowing down to: paying homage, kneeling before
decisions.reason: The verb is used for bowing before a king or for worship. Here it is mocking homage.

decisions.choice: were striking, were spitting, were bowing: repeated actions
decisions.reason: The tenses show the soldiers doing these things again and again.

decisions.choice: spitting on him: as Jesus said and as the servant of Isaiah suffered
decisions.reason: Jesus said the Gentiles would spit on him (10:34). Isaiah 50:6 speaks of one who did not hide his face from spitting.

decisions.choice: as if he were a king
decisions.reason: Readable makes the mockery clear.

decisions.choice: "cây sậy" (L); "gậy" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision gives "a stick or cane"; Vietnamese "cây sậy" would suggest a soft grass stem, so Balanced and Readable say "gậy".

decisions.choice: "갈대" (L); "갈대 막대기" (B); "막대기" (R), here and in 15:36
decisions.reason: A reed is a stick or cane (meaning decision); Balanced keeps the plant and says how it was used.

decisions.choice: caña (L); vara (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is a reed or a cane (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "caña"; Balanced and Readable say "vara", since a reed that strikes hard is a stick. The same words are used in 15:36.

decisions.choice: como si fuera un rey (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says that the kneeling was mock homage (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: ils lui frappaient la tête (L); ils le frappaient à la tête (B, R), with the span on "lui" or "le"
decisions.reason: With a part of the body French says "lui ... la tête" or "le frapper à la tête" rather than "sa tête", so the deity_pronoun span goes on "lui" or "le" where the English has it on "his", as in John 19:33.

decisions.choice: mwanzi (L); fimbo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a reed or cane (meaning decision). Literal says "mwanzi" (reed, cane); Balanced and Readable say "fimbo" (stick), as the English says "stick". The same in 15:36.

source.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ, ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν πορφύραν καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια τὰ ἴδια.

records.literal_gloss: And when they had mocked him, they took off him the purple and put on him the garments his own.

en.L: And when they had mocked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they took the purple off {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own garments on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: When they had finished mocking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they stripped the purple robe off {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and dressed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own clothes.
en.R: When the soldiers were done making fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they took off the purple robe. They put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own clothes back on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và khi đã chế nhạo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong, họ cởi [áo] màu tía khỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và mặc lại áo xống của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Chế nhạo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong, họ lột áo choàng tía ra và mặc lại quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Khi những người lính chế giễu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xong, họ cởi áo choàng màu tía ra. Họ mặc lại quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 그분을 조롱하고 나서, 그분에게서 자주색 옷을 벗기고 그분 자신의 겉옷을 입혔다.
ko.B: 이렇게 예수를 조롱하고 나서, 자주색 옷을 벗기고 예수의 옷을 도로 입혔다.
ko.R: 병사들은 실컷 예수를 놀리고 나서 자주색 옷을 벗겼다. 그리고 예수의 옷을 다시 입혔다.

es.L: Y cuando se burlaron de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, le quitaron la púrpura y le pusieron sus propias ropas.
es.B: Cuando terminaron de burlarse de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, le quitaron el manto de púrpura y lo vistieron con su propia ropa.
es.R: Cuando los soldados terminaron de burlarse de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, le quitaron el manto de color púrpura. Le volvieron a poner su propia ropa.

fr.L: Et quand ils se furent moqués de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ôtèrent la pourpre et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} revêtirent de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} propres vêtements.
fr.B: Quand ils eurent fini de se moquer de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} enlevèrent le manteau pourpre et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} remirent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements.
fr.R: Quand les soldats ont fini de se moquer de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont enlevé le manteau pourpre. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont remis {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} propres vêtements.

sw.L: Na walipokwisha kumdhihaki, walimvua ile zambarau, wakamvika mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}.
sw.B: Walipomaliza kumdhihaki, walimvua lile vazi la zambarau, wakamvika nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.
sw.R: Askari walipomaliza kumfanyia mzaha, walimvua lile vazi la zambarau. Wakamvalisha tena nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.

decisions.choice: mocked: the passion prediction fulfilled
decisions.reason: Jesus said the Gentiles would mock him (10:34). Mark uses the same verb.

decisions.choice: garments: his outer clothes
decisions.reason: The word means clothing, especially the outer robe. These are divided in 15:24.

decisions.choice: the purple robe
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the noun Greek leaves implied.

decisions.choice: "조롱하다" (L, B); "놀리다" (R) for empaizo, here and in 15:31
decisions.reason: The verb of Jesus' prediction in 10:34; "희롱하다" is the older church word and now suggests sexual harassment.

decisions.choice: el manto (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable say what was purple, as in 15:17. "Burlarse de" is the verb of the passion prediction (meaning decision m1).

source.text: καὶ ἐξάγουσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα σταυρώσωσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And they lead out him that they might crucify him.

en.L: And they lead {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out to crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Then they took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out to crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then they led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of the city to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on a cross.

vi.L: Và họ dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra để đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Rồi họ dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ra để đóng đinh.
vi.R: Rồi họ dẫn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra khỏi thành để đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên cây thập tự.

ko.L: 그리고 그분을 십자가에 못 박으려고 밖으로 끌고 나간다.
ko.B: 그리고 십자가에 못 박으려고 예수를 끌고 나갔다.
ko.R: 그리고 십자가에 못 박으려고 예수를 성 밖으로 끌고 나갔다.

es.L: Y lo sacan para crucificarlo.
es.B: Luego lo sacaron para crucificarlo.
es.R: Luego lo sacaron de la ciudad para clavarlo en una cruz.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmènent dehors pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifier.
fr.B: Puis ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}emmenèrent pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifier.
fr.R: Puis ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont emmené hors de la ville pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} clouer sur une croix.

sw.L: Na wanamtoa nje ili wamsulubishe.
sw.B: Kisha wakamtoa nje ili wamsulubishe.
sw.R: Kisha wakampeleka nje ya mji ili wampigilie misumari msalabani.

decisions.choice: they lead out: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, the sense is past.

decisions.choice: led out: outside the city
decisions.reason: Executions took place outside the city walls (Hebrews 13:12).

decisions.choice: out of the city
decisions.reason: Readable says where they took him; Hebrews 13:12 says Jesus suffered outside the gate.

decisions.choice: de la ciudad (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: executions were held outside the city (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps Mark's present "sacan".

source.text: Καὶ ἀγγαρεύουσιν παράγοντά τινα Σίμωνα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον ἀπ’ ἀγροῦ, τὸν πατέρα Ἀλεξάνδρου καὶ Ῥούφου, ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And they compel passing by someone Simon a Cyrenian coming from [the] country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, that he might carry the cross of him.

en.L: And they compel a certain passerby, Simon, a Cyrenian, coming from [the] country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cross.
en.B: A man named Simon from Cyrene was coming in from the countryside and passing by; he was the father of Alexander and Rufus. The soldiers pressed him into carrying the cross for Jesus.
en.R: A man named Simon was walking by, coming into the city from the fields. He was from Cyrene in North Africa, and he was the father of Alexander and Rufus. The soldiers made him carry Jesus' cross.

vi.L: Và họ bắt một người đi ngang qua, là Si-môn, người Sy-ren, đang từ ngoài đồng về, cha của A-léc-xan-đơ và Ru-phu, phải vác cây thập tự của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Có một người tên Si-môn, quê ở Sy-ren, từ ngoài đồng vào thành và đang đi ngang qua đó; ông là cha của A-léc-xan-đơ và Ru-phu. Lính bắt ông phải vác cây thập tự thay cho Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Có một người tên Si-môn đang đi ngang qua. Ông từ ngoài đồng đi vào thành. Ông quê ở Sy-ren, một thành ở Bắc Phi, và là cha của A-léc-xan-đơ và Ru-phu. Những người lính bắt ông vác cây thập tự của Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 시골에서 오다가 지나가는 어떤 사람, 곧 알렉산더와 루포의 아버지인 구레네 사람 시몬에게 억지로 그분의 십자가를 지게 한다.
ko.B: 그때 구레네 사람 시몬이 시골에서 들어오다가 그곳을 지나가고 있었다. 그는 알렉산더와 루포의 아버지였다. 병사들은 그에게 억지로 예수의 십자가를 지게 했다.
ko.R: 그때 시몬이라는 사람이 밭에서 성안으로 들어오다가 그 곁을 지나가고 있었다. 그는 북아프리카의 구레네에서 온 사람이었고, 알렉산더와 루포의 아버지였다. 병사들은 시몬에게 억지로 예수의 십자가를 지고 가게 했다.

es.L: Y obligan a uno que pasaba, un tal Simón, cireneo, que venía del campo, el padre de Alejandro y de Rufo, a que llevara su cruz.
es.B: Un hombre de Cirene llamado Simón, padre de Alejandro y de Rufo, pasaba por allí al volver del campo, y los soldados lo obligaron a cargar con la cruz de Jesús.
es.R: Un hombre llamado Simón pasaba por allí. Venía del campo a la ciudad. Era de Cirene, en el norte de África, y era el padre de Alejandro y de Rufo. Los soldados lo obligaron a cargar la cruz de Jesús.

fr.L: Et ils réquisitionnent un passant, un certain Simon, Cyrénéen, qui venait des champs, le père d’Alexandre et de Rufus, pour qu’il porte {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} croix.
fr.B: Un homme de Cyrène, Simon, passait par là en revenant des champs ; c’était le père d’Alexandre et de Rufus. Les soldats le réquisitionnèrent pour porter la croix de Jésus.
fr.R: Un homme qui s’appelait Simon passait par là. Il revenait des champs et entrait dans la ville. Il était de Cyrène, en Afrique du Nord, et c’était le père d’Alexandre et de Rufus. Les soldats l’ont obligé à porter la croix de Jésus.

sw.L: Na wanamlazimisha mpita njia mmoja, Simoni Mkirene, aliyekuwa akitoka shambani, baba yao Aleksanda na Rufo, aubebe msalaba {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Mtu mmoja aitwaye Simoni, wa Kirene, alikuwa akipita akitoka mashambani; yeye alikuwa baba yao Aleksanda na Rufo. Askari wakamlazimisha aubebe msalaba wa Yesu.
sw.R: Mtu mmoja aitwaye Simoni alikuwa akipita, akiingia mjini kutoka mashambani. Alikuwa mwenyeji wa Kirene, mji wa Afrika ya Kaskazini, naye alikuwa baba yao Aleksanda na Rufo. Askari wakamlazimisha aubebe msalaba wa Yesu.

decisions.choice: compel: force into service, as Roman soldiers could
decisions.reason: Roman soldiers had the right to make a civilian carry a load for them. Jesus speaks of this in Matthew 5:41.

decisions.choice: Cyrenian: from Cyrene, a city in North Africa with a large Jewish community
decisions.reason: Jews from Cyrene had their own synagogue in Jerusalem (Acts 6:9). Simon may have come for Passover or lived in the area.

decisions.choice: the father of Alexander and Rufus: men Mark's readers knew
decisions.reason: Mark names the sons as if his readers knew them. A Rufus in the church at Rome is greeted in Romans 16:13; he may be the same man, but that cannot be shown.

decisions.choice: the cross: the crossbeam carried by the condemned man
decisions.reason: The condemned man usually carried the crossbeam to the place of execution. Jesus, weakened by the flogging, could not.

decisions.choice: they compel: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: The sense is past.

decisions.choice: The soldiers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject. Readable also says where Cyrene was.

decisions.choice: "Sy-ren", "A-léc-xan-đơ", "Ru-phu"
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliterations, following the tradition settled for names (docs/vietnamese-style.md, "Settled").

decisions.choice: "cây thập tự"
decisions.reason: The plain Protestant word, as in John 19:17.

decisions.choice: Protestant name forms: "구레네", "알렉산더", "루포"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant forms (style guide, section 5); the Catholic and Common Translation forms are the alternatives.

decisions.choice: los soldados (B, R); la cruz de Jesús (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable name the soldiers, who could force a passer-by into service (meaning decision m1), and name Jesus, since "su cruz" after Simon could be misread. "Cargar" is the verb of John 19:17 Spanish. Literal keeps the Greek word for Simon's origin, "cireneo".

decisions.choice: réquisitionner (L, B); obliger (R)
decisions.reason: "Réquisitionner" is the French word for forcing someone into service by authority, which is what Roman soldiers could do (meaning decision m1); Readable uses the everyday "obliger".

decisions.choice: Simoni Mkirene (L), Simoni wa Kirene (B, R); Aleksanda; Rufo
decisions.reason: The names in their usual Swahili forms. "Mkirene" is the ordinary Swahili way to name a man of Cyrene, as "Mnazareti" is a man of Nazareth; Balanced and Readable say where he came from, and Readable adds where Cyrene was, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Γολγοθᾶν τόπον, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Κρανίου Τόπος.

records.literal_gloss: And they bring him to the Golgotha place, which is being translated, Of a Skull Place.

en.L: And they bring {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the place Golgotha, which is translated, Place of a Skull.
en.B: They brought Jesus to a place named Golgotha, meaning Place of a Skull.
en.R: They took Jesus to a place called Golgotha. That name means "the Place of the Skull."

vi.L: Và họ đem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến chỗ Gô-gô-tha, dịch ra là Nơi Cái Sọ.
vi.B: Họ đưa Đức Giê-xu đến một nơi gọi là Gô-gô-tha, nghĩa là Nơi Cái Sọ.
vi.R: Họ đưa Đức Giê-xu đến một nơi gọi là Gô-gô-tha. Tên ấy có nghĩa là "Cái Sọ".

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그분을 골고다라는 곳으로 데리고 간다. 그것은 번역하면 해골의 곳이다.
ko.B: 그들은 예수를 골고다라는 곳으로 데리고 갔다. 골고다는 해골 터라는 뜻이다.
ko.R: 그들은 예수를 골고다라는 곳으로 데리고 갔다. 그 이름은 "해골 터"라는 뜻이다.

es.L: Y lo llevan al lugar Gólgota, que traducido significa Lugar de la Calavera.
es.B: Llevaron a Jesús a un lugar llamado Gólgota, que significa Lugar de la Calavera.
es.R: Llevaron a Jesús a un lugar llamado Gólgota. Ese nombre quiere decir «Lugar de la Calavera».

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}amènent au lieu [nommé] Golgotha, ce qui se traduit : Lieu du Crâne.
fr.B: Ils conduisirent Jésus à un endroit nommé Golgotha, ce qui signifie Lieu du Crâne.
fr.R: Ils ont emmené Jésus à un endroit appelé Golgotha. Ce nom veut dire « le Lieu du Crâne ».

sw.L: Na wanamleta mahali pa Golgotha, ambapo kwa tafsiri ni Mahali pa Fuvu.
sw.B: Walimpeleka Yesu mahali paitwapo Golgotha, maana yake Mahali pa Fuvu.
sw.R: Walimpeleka Yesu mahali palipoitwa Golgotha. Jina hilo maana yake ni "Mahali pa Fuvu."

decisions.choice: Golgotha: an Aramaic word for skull
decisions.reason: Mark gives the Aramaic name and then its meaning, as he does with other Aramaic words (5:41; 7:34).

decisions.choice: Place of a Skull: why it had this name is not known
decisions.reason: The name may come from the shape of the hill or rock, or from its use for executions. The Gospels place it outside the city near a road (15:29; John 19:20).

decisions.choice: they bring: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: The sense is past.

decisions.choice: That name means
decisions.reason: Readable makes a new sentence for Mark's explanation.

decisions.choice: "Gô-gô-tha"; "Nơi Cái Sọ" (L, B), "Cái Sọ" (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 19:17: the name is translated literally; "Đồi Sọ" adds a hill that Mark does not mention.

decisions.choice: "골고다" at every level; "해골의 곳" (L), "해골 터" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The forms of the Korean John 19:17.

decisions.choice: Gólgota; Lugar de la Calavera
decisions.reason: As in John 19:17 Spanish: "Calavera" is the Spanish word for a skull, and Mark gives his own translation of the name (meaning decision m1); "Calvario" comes from the Latin and is not in the Greek.

decisions.choice: Lieu du Crâne (every level)
decisions.reason: As in John 19:17, each level gives Mark's own translation of the name, with capitals as a place name; "Calvaire" comes from the Latin word for skull and is not in the Greek.

decisions.choice: Mahali pa Fuvu, at every level
decisions.reason: As in Swahili John 19:17: Mark translates the name for his readers (meaning decision), so each level gives the local name and then its meaning, "Mahali pa Fuvu" (the place of a skull). "Kalvari" comes from the Latin and is not in the Greek.

source.text: καὶ ἐδίδουν αὐτῷ ἐσμυρνισμένον οἶνον, ὃς δὲ οὐκ ἔλαβεν.

records.literal_gloss: And they were giving him having been mixed with myrrh wine; but he not took.

en.L: And they were offering {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} wine mixed with myrrh, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not take [it].
en.B: They tried to give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} wine flavored with myrrh, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not take it.
en.R: They offered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} wine mixed with myrrh, a bitter spice. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not drink it.

vi.L: Và họ đưa cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rượu pha một dược, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không nhận.
vi.B: Họ muốn cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} uống rượu pha một dược, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không chịu uống.
vi.R: Họ đưa cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rượu pha một dược, là một thứ hương liệu đắng. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không uống.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 몰약을 탄 포도주를 그분께 주고 있었다. 그러나 그분은 받지 않으셨다.
ko.B: 그들은 몰약을 탄 포도주를 예수께 주려 했으나, 예수께서는 받지 않으셨다.
ko.R: 그들은 몰약이라는 쓴 향료를 섞은 포도주를 예수께 주었다. 그러나 예수께서는 그것을 마시지 않으셨다.

es.L: Y le daban vino mezclado con mirra, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no [lo] tomó.
es.B: Trataron de darle vino mezclado con mirra, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no lo quiso tomar.
es.R: Le ofrecieron vino mezclado con mirra, una especia amarga. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no quiso beberlo.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donnaient du vin mêlé de myrrhe, mais {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ne [le] prit pas.
fr.B: Ils voulurent {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donner du vin parfumé à la myrrhe, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} refusa de le prendre.
fr.R: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont offert du vin mélangé avec de la myrrhe, une épice amère. Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a pas voulu le boire.

sw.L: Na walikuwa wakimpa divai iliyochanganywa na manemane, lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakuipokea.
sw.B: Walijaribu kumpa divai iliyotiwa manemane, lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakuikubali.
sw.R: Walimpa divai iliyochanganywa na manemane, kiungo kichungu. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakukubali kuinywa.

decisions.choice: wine mixed with myrrh: perhaps a drink to dull the pain
alternatives: a drink meant to mock him
a costly wine given as an honor
decisions.reason: Proverbs 31:6 says to give strong drink to one who is perishing, and Jewish tradition tells of women in Jerusalem who gave a drugged drink to the condemned. Myrrh also flavored fine wine. Mark does not say why it was given.

decisions.choice: were offering: they tried to give
decisions.reason: The tense shows an attempt. He refused.

decisions.choice: he did not take it: Jesus refuses what would dull his suffering
decisions.reason: At the last supper Jesus said he would not drink wine again until the kingdom of God (14:25). He also goes to death fully aware.

decisions.choice: a bitter spice
decisions.reason: Readable says what myrrh was.

decisions.choice: Trataron de darle (B)
decisions.reason: As in English: the imperfect means they offered it and he did not take it (meaning decision m2). The Greek names Jesus with a pronoun at the turn of the sentence, so Spanish keeps the stressed "él" with the setting.

decisions.choice: una especia amarga (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what myrrh was (meaning decision m1).

source.text: καὶ σταυροῦσιν αὐτὸν καὶ διαμερίζονται τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντες κλῆρον ἐπ’ αὐτὰ τίς τί ἄρῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And they crucify him and they divide the garments of him, casting a lot for them, who what should take.

en.L: And they crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and divide {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments, casting lots for them [to see] who should take what.
en.B: Then they crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They shared out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes by throwing dice for them to see what each would get.
en.R: Then the soldiers nailed Jesus to the cross. They divided {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes among themselves. They threw dice to decide who would get each piece.

vi.L: Và họ đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và chia nhau áo xống của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, bắt thăm [xem] ai lấy cái gì.
vi.B: Rồi họ đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và chia nhau quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, bắt thăm để xem mỗi người được cái gì.
vi.R: Rồi những người lính đóng đinh Đức Giê-xu trên cây thập tự. Họ chia nhau quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ bắt thăm để định ai được món nào.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그분을 십자가에 못 박는다. 그리고 그분의 겉옷들을 나누는데, 누가 무엇을 가질지 [정하려고] 그것들을 두고 제비를 뽑는다.
ko.B: 그리고 그들은 예수를 십자가에 못 박았다. 그리고 각자 무엇을 가질지 제비를 뽑아 예수의 옷을 나누어 가졌다.
ko.R: 병사들은 예수를 십자가에 못 박았다. 그리고 예수의 옷을 자기들끼리 나누어 가졌다. 누가 어느 옷을 가질지 제비를 뽑아 정했다.

es.L: Y lo crucifican, y se reparten sus ropas, echando suertes sobre ellas [para ver] qué se llevaría cada uno.
es.B: Entonces lo crucificaron y se repartieron su ropa, echando suertes para ver qué le tocaba a cada uno.
es.R: Luego los soldados lo clavaron en la cruz. Se repartieron su ropa entre ellos. Hicieron un sorteo para decidir quién se quedaba con cada prenda.

fr.L: Et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifient et se partagent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements, en jetant le sort sur eux [pour savoir] qui prendrait quoi.
fr.B: Puis ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifièrent et se partagèrent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements, en les tirant au sort pour savoir ce que chacun prendrait.
fr.R: Puis les soldats ont cloué Jésus sur la croix. Ils se sont partagé {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements. Ils ont tiré au sort pour savoir qui aurait chaque vêtement.

sw.L: Na wanamsulubisha, na wanagawana mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wakiyatupia kura [kuona] nani achukue nini.
sw.B: Kisha wakamsulubisha. Wakagawana nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kwa kuzitupia kura, ili kuona kila mmoja atapata nini.
sw.R: Kisha askari wakampigilia Yesu misumari msalabani. Wakagawana nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Waliamua kwa bahati nani apate kipande gani.

decisions.choice: they divide his garments, casting lots: Psalm 22:19
decisions.reason: The psalm says: they divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots. Mark uses the psalm's words without saying he quotes it.

decisions.choice: casting lots: throwing marked stones or dice to decide
decisions.reason: Lots were small objects thrown to make a choice by chance.

decisions.choice: dividing the garments: the executioners kept the clothes of the condemned
decisions.reason: The condemned were crucified naked or nearly so, and their clothes went to the soldiers.

decisions.choice: they crucify, they divide: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark tells the crucifixion itself in a few plain words. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: throwing dice (B); threw dice (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a familiar game of chance for lots.

decisions.choice: "bắt thăm" at every level
alternatives: "gieo xúc xắc" (B, R, like the English "dice")
decisions.reason: "bắt thăm" is the plain Vietnamese word for deciding by lot and keeps the echo of Psalm 22, as in John 19:24; dice are a modern picture.

decisions.choice: "제비를 뽑다" at every level
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean John 19:24, and of Psalm 22 that the verse echoes; Korean readers know the custom, so Balanced and Readable do not need the English "dice".

decisions.choice: echando suertes (L, B); hicieron un sorteo (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 19:24 Spanish, the same psalm words (meaning decision m1): Literal and Balanced keep the phrase of Psalm 22, and Readable uses the everyday word for deciding by chance, without naming a game the text does not name (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: jeter le sort (L); tirer au sort (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "tirer au sort" covers casting lots without naming a game the text does not name (meaning decision m2), so French does not follow the English "dice". Literal keeps "jeter le sort", the wording of Psalm 22:19 in the French of John 19:24, so that the allusion can be seen (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: kutupa kura (L, B); kuamua kwa bahati (R)
decisions.reason: As in Swahili John 19:24: lots were thrown to let chance decide (meaning decision). "Kutupa kura" keeps the picture of Psalm 22, which Mark echoes; "kupiga kura" today usually means to vote, so Readable says "kuamua kwa bahati" (decide by chance). The English "dice" is not followed with "kete", which names a game.

source.text: Ἦν δὲ ὥρα τρίτη καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Now it was [the] hour third and they crucified him.

en.L: Now it was the third hour, and they crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: It was nine in the morning when they crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: It was about nine o'clock in the morning when they nailed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the cross.

vi.L: Lúc ấy là giờ thứ ba, và họ đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Lúc họ đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là chín giờ sáng.
vi.R: Lúc họ đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên cây thập tự là khoảng chín giờ sáng.

ko.L: 그때는 셋째 시였고, 그들이 그분을 십자가에 못 박았다.
ko.B: 그들이 예수를 십자가에 못 박은 것은 오전 아홉 시였다.
ko.R: 예수께서 십자가에 못 박히신 때는 오전 아홉 시쯤이었다.

es.L: Era la hora tercera, y lo crucificaron.
es.B: Eran las nueve de la mañana cuando lo crucificaron.
es.R: Eran como las nueve de la mañana cuando lo clavaron en la cruz.

fr.L: Or c’était la troisième heure, et ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifièrent.
fr.B: Il était neuf heures du matin quand ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifièrent.
fr.R: Il était environ neuf heures du matin quand ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont cloué sur la croix.

sw.L: Basi ilikuwa saa tatu, nao wakamsulubisha.
sw.B: Ilikuwa saa tatu asubuhi walipomsulubisha.
sw.R: Ilikuwa yapata saa tatu asubuhi walipompigilia misumari msalabani.

decisions.choice: the third hour: about nine in the morning
decisions.reason: Jews and Romans counted the hours of daylight from sunrise, about six in the morning. The third hour was about nine. Mark marks the day in three-hour steps: the third, sixth and ninth hours (15:33-34).

decisions.choice: the third hour: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "sixth", making Mark agree with John 19:14, where Jesus is still before Pilate at about the sixth hour. The SBLGNT reads "third". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: and: when, the time when they crucified him
decisions.reason: The "and" links the time with the event: it was the third hour when they crucified him.

decisions.choice: nine in the morning (B); about nine o'clock in the morning (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the ancient way of counting the hours. Balanced and Readable give the time as we count it, since the third hour after sunrise was about nine o'clock.

decisions.choice: "셋째 시" (L); "오전 아홉 시" (B, R); likewise "여섯째 시", "아홉째 시" (L) and "낮 열두 시", "오후 세 시" (B, R) in 15:33-34
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek count, Balanced and Readable give the modern time (style guide, section 5), as the Korean John 19:14 does.

decisions.choice: la hora tercera (L); las nueve de la mañana (B); como las nueve de la mañana (R)
decisions.reason: The choice of John 4:6 and 19:14 Spanish for clock times: Literal keeps the hour as counted then, Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m1). The same in 15:33-34.

decisions.choice: la troisième heure (L); neuf heures du matin (B, R), and so midi and quinze heures in 15:33-34
alternatives: la troisième heure at every level
decisions.reason: The French choice for clock times in the Gospels, as in John 19:14: Literal keeps the hour counted from sunrise, Balanced and Readable give the modern time (meaning decision m1). Readable says "trois heures de l'après-midi" in 15:33-34, which young readers find plainer than "quinze heures".

decisions.choice: saa tatu at every level (also saa sita, saa tisa in 15:33-34)
decisions.reason: Mark counts the hours from sunrise, and so does Swahili time, so "the third hour" is simply "saa tatu" (about nine in the morning, meaning decision) and needs no conversion, unlike the English. Balanced and Readable add "asubuhi" (in the morning).

source.text: καὶ ἦν ἡ ἐπιγραφὴ τῆς αἰτίας αὐτοῦ ἐπιγεγραμμένη· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

records.literal_gloss: And there was the inscription of the charge of him having been inscribed, The King of the Jews.

en.L: And the inscription of the charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was inscribed: "The King of the Jews."
en.B: The written charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} said, "The King of the Jews."
en.R: A sign was put up that told why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was being killed. It said, "The King of the Jews."

vi.L: Và bản ghi tội trạng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được viết: "Vua của người Do Thái."
vi.B: Tấm bảng ghi tội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} viết: "Vua dân Do Thái."
vi.R: Người ta treo một tấm bảng cho biết vì sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bị xử tử. Trên đó ghi: "Vua dân Do Thái."

ko.L: 그리고 그분의 죄목을 적은 패에는 "유대인의 왕"이라고 쓰여 있었다.
ko.B: 예수의 죄패에는 "유대인의 왕"이라고 쓰여 있었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 왜 죽임을 당하시는지 알리는 팻말도 붙어 있었다. 거기에는 "유대인의 왕"이라고 쓰여 있었다.

es.L: Y estaba escrita la inscripción de su causa: «El Rey de los judíos».
es.B: El letrero con el motivo de su condena decía: «El Rey de los judíos».
es.R: Pusieron un cartel que decía por qué lo estaban matando: «El Rey de los judíos».

fr.L: Et l’inscription de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} condamnation était inscrite : « Le roi des Juifs. »
fr.B: L’écriteau qui donnait le motif de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} condamnation portait : « Le roi des Juifs. »
fr.R: On avait mis une pancarte qui disait pourquoi on {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} mettait à mort. Elle disait : « Le roi des Juifs. »

sw.L: Na maandishi ya shtaka {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} yalikuwa yameandikwa: "Mfalme wa Wayahudi."
sw.B: Tangazo la shtaka {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} liliandikwa: "Mfalme wa Wayahudi."
sw.R: Kibao kiliwekwa kuonyesha kwa nini alikuwa akiuawa. Kiliandikwa, "Mfalme wa Wayahudi."

decisions.choice: the inscription of the charge: a notice giving the crime
decisions.reason: The Romans made the reason for an execution known, on a board carried before the man or fixed to the cross.

decisions.choice: The King of the Jews: the charge on which Jesus died
decisions.reason: It was meant as mockery and as a warning, but for Mark it states the truth about Jesus in the mouth of his enemies.

decisions.choice: a sign that told why he was being killed
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the notice was.

decisions.choice: "죄목을 적은 패" (L); "죄패" (B); "팻말" (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's word names the charge; Balanced uses the Korean word for a notice of the crime (as the Korean John 19:19 Balanced), and Readable the everyday "팻말".

decisions.choice: la inscripción de su causa (L); el letrero con el motivo de su condena (B); un cartel (R)
decisions.reason: A notice that gave the crime (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the legal sense of "causa", as Pilate's "ninguna causa" in John 19:4; Balanced and Readable use "letrero" and "cartel", the words of John 19:19 Spanish.

decisions.choice: l'inscription ... inscrite, sa condamnation (L); l'écriteau (B); une pancarte (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek doubling of "inscription" and "inscribed". The notice gave the crime for which he was condemned (meaning decision m1); "sa condamnation" says that more plainly in French than "son accusation". Balanced and Readable use the words of John 19:19 for the board itself.

decisions.choice: maandishi ya shtaka (L); tangazo la shtaka (B); kibao (R)
decisions.reason: A notice giving the crime (meaning decision). Literal keeps "maandishi" (writing), which repeats the Greek play of inscription and inscribed; Balanced uses "tangazo" (public notice) and Readable "kibao" (a board with writing), the words of Swahili John 19:19.

source.text: καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ σταυροῦσιν δύο λῃστάς, ἕνα ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ ἕνα ἐξ εὐωνύμων αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And with him they crucify two bandits, one at [the] right and one at [the] left of him.

en.L: And with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} they crucify two bandits, one on [the] right and one on [the] left of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They also crucified two bandits with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, one at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right and one at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.
en.R: Two robbers were also nailed to crosses next to Jesus, one on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right side and one on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.

vi.L: Và cùng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, họ đóng đinh hai kẻ cướp, một [kẻ] bên phải và một [kẻ] bên trái {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Họ cũng đóng đinh hai kẻ cướp cùng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, một kẻ bên phải, một kẻ bên trái {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Có hai tên cướp cũng bị đóng đinh trên cây thập tự cạnh Đức Giê-xu, một tên ở bên phải, một tên ở bên trái {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그분과 함께 강도 두 사람을 십자가에 못 박는다. 하나는 [그분의] 오른쪽에, 하나는 그분의 왼쪽에 [못 박는다].
ko.B: 그들은 강도 두 사람도 예수와 함께 십자가에 못 박았다. 한 사람은 예수의 오른쪽에, 또 한 사람은 왼쪽에 못 박았다.
ko.R: 강도 두 사람도 예수 곁에서 십자가에 못 박혔다. 한 사람은 예수의 오른쪽에, 다른 한 사람은 왼쪽에 있었다.

es.L: Y con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} crucifican a dos bandidos, uno a [la] derecha y otro a su izquierda.
es.B: Con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} crucificaron también a dos bandidos, uno a su derecha y otro a su izquierda.
es.R: También clavaron en cruces a dos ladrones junto a Jesús, uno a su derecha y otro a su izquierda.

fr.L: Et avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ils crucifient deux bandits, un à droite et un à gauche de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ils crucifièrent aussi deux bandits, l’un à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} droite et l’autre à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gauche.
fr.R: On a aussi cloué deux bandits sur des croix à côté de Jésus, l’un à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} droite et l’autre à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gauche.

sw.L: Na pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} wanawasulubisha wanyang'anyi wawili, mmoja kulia na mmoja kushoto {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Pia walisulubisha wanyang'anyi wawili pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, mmoja upande {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia na mwingine upande {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kushoto.
sw.R: Wanyang'anyi wawili nao walipigiliwa misumari kwenye misalaba karibu na Yesu, mmoja upande {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia na mwingine upande {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kushoto.

decisions.choice: bandits: armed robbers, a word also used for rebels
decisions.reason: The word means a violent robber. Roman and Jewish writers also used it for those who took up arms against Rome, like the rebels of 15:7. Jesus used it in 14:48.

decisions.choice: one on the right and one on the left: the places James and John asked for
decisions.reason: James and John asked to sit at Jesus' right and left in his glory (10:37, 40). Mark uses the same phrase here.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 28
alternatives: add verse 28: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, And he was counted with the lawless
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add here: "And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, And he was counted with the lawless." The words come from Isaiah 53:12, which Jesus quotes in Luke 22:37. The earliest manuscripts lack the verse, and Mark rarely quotes Scripture this way himself, so it is likely a later addition taken from Luke. Verse 28 is skipped in the numbering for this reason. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: they crucify: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: The sense is past.

decisions.choice: robbers
decisions.reason: Readable uses the common word. Literal and Balanced keep "bandits", which leaves room for the sense of armed rebels.

decisions.choice: "강도" for lestes at every level
decisions.reason: The word of the Korean John 18:40; Korean "강도" is an armed robber, which also suits the rebels the word can describe (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: bandidos (L, B); ladrones (R)
decisions.reason: The word is used of armed robbers and also of rebels (meaning decision m1); "bandidos" keeps both. Readable says "ladrones", the everyday word, as the English says "robbers".

decisions.choice: des bandits (every level)
decisions.reason: The word means armed robbers and was also used of rebels (meaning decision m1). "Bandit" is the everyday French word for a violent outlaw, the word chosen in John 18:40, and is plain enough for Readable, so French keeps one word where the English Readable says "robbers".

decisions.choice: wanyang'anyi at every level
decisions.reason: "Mnyang'anyi" is a robber who takes by force, the word Swahili John uses for Barabbas (18:40). "Wezi" (thieves) would make them petty thieves; the possible sense of rebels belongs to the meaning notes. Swahili needs no bracketed "[the]" before right and left.

source.text: Καὶ οἱ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ λέγοντες· Οὐὰ ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ οἰκοδομῶν ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις, σῶσον σεαυτὸν καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And those passing by were blaspheming him, shaking the heads of them and saying, Aha, the [one] destroying the temple and building [it] in three days, \v 30 save yourself, having come down from the cross.

en.L: And those passing by were blaspheming {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, shaking their heads and saying, "Aha! You who destroy the temple and build [it] in three days, \v 30 save {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} by coming down from the cross!"
en.B: People who went by hurled insults at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, wagging their heads. "Ha!" they said. "So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were going to tear down the temple and raise it again in three days! \v 30 Then save {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} by coming down from the cross!"
en.R: People walking by shook their heads and shouted insults at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said, "Look at {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! You said {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would destroy the temple and build it again in three days. \v 30 So save {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}! Come down from the cross!"

vi.L: Và những người đi ngang qua phỉ báng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, lắc đầu và nói: "Ha! Ông là kẻ phá đền thờ và xây [lại] trong ba ngày, \v 30 hãy tự cứu mình bằng cách xuống khỏi cây thập tự đi!"
vi.B: Những người qua lại buông lời nhục mạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vừa lắc đầu vừa nói: "Ha! Ông định phá đền thờ rồi xây lại trong ba ngày kia mà! \v 30 Vậy hãy tự cứu mình, xuống khỏi cây thập tự đi!"
vi.R: Những người đi ngang qua lắc đầu và lớn tiếng sỉ nhục {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ nói: "Nhìn ông kìa! Ông nói ông sẽ phá đền thờ rồi xây lại trong ba ngày. \v 30 Vậy hãy tự cứu mình đi! Xuống khỏi cây thập tự đi!"

ko.L: 그리고 지나가는 사람들이 자기들의 머리를 흔들며 그분을 모독하여 말했다. "아하, 성전을 허물고 사흘 만에 짓는다는 자여, \v 30 십자가에서 내려와서 너 자신이나 구원하여라!"
ko.B: 지나가는 사람들도 머리를 흔들며 예수께 욕설을 퍼부었다. "하! 성전을 허물고 사흘 만에 다시 세우겠다더니! \v 30 그렇다면 십자가에서 내려와서 너 자신이나 구원해 보아라!"
ko.R: 지나가던 사람들은 머리를 흔들며 예수께 욕을 했다. 그들이 말했다. "꼴좋다! 너는 성전을 허물고 사흘 만에 다시 짓겠다고 했지? \v 30 그러면 너 자신이나 구해 보아라! 십자가에서 내려와 보아라!"

es.L: Y los que pasaban lo insultaban, meneando la cabeza y diciendo: «¡Ah, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} que destruyes el templo y [lo] edificas en tres días, \v 30 sálvate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo bajando de la cruz!».
es.B: Los que pasaban lo cubrían de insultos y meneaban la cabeza. «¡Ja!», decían. «¡Así que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} ibas a derribar el templo y a reconstruirlo en tres días! \v 30 ¡Pues sálvate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo y baja de la cruz!».
es.R: La gente que pasaba por allí meneaba la cabeza y le gritaba insultos. Le decían: «¡Mírate! Decías que ibas a destruir el templo y a construirlo otra vez en tres días. \v 30 ¡Pues sálvate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo! ¡Baja de la cruz!».

fr.L: Et les passants blasphémaient contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, hochant la tête et disant : « Ha ! Toi qui détruis le temple et [le] rebâtis en trois jours, \v 30 sauve-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} en descendant de la croix ! »
fr.B: Les passants {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}insultaient en hochant la tête : « Ha ! disaient-ils, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui devais détruire le temple et le rebâtir en trois jours ! \v 30 Alors sauve-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} en descendant de la croix ! »
fr.R: Les gens qui passaient secouaient la tête et lançaient des insultes à Jésus. Ils disaient : « Regarde-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ! Tu disais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} allais détruire le temple et le reconstruire en trois jours. \v 30 Alors sauve-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ! Descends de la croix ! »

sw.L: Na wale waliokuwa wakipita walikuwa wakimtukana, wakitikisa vichwa vyao na kusema, "Aha! Wewe unayelivunja hekalu na kulijenga kwa siku tatu, \v 30 jiokoe {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kwa kushuka kutoka msalabani!"
sw.B: Watu waliopita njiani walimtukana, wakitikisa vichwa vyao. "Aha!" walisema. "Wewe ndiye ambaye ungelibomoa hekalu na kulijenga tena kwa siku tatu! \v 30 Basi jiokoe {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}; shuka kutoka msalabani!"
sw.R: Watu waliokuwa wakipita walitikisa vichwa vyao na kumtukana. Walisema, "Jitazame sasa! Ulisema utalibomoa hekalu na kulijenga tena kwa siku tatu. \v 30 Basi jiokoe {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}! Shuka kutoka msalabani!"

decisions.choice: blaspheming: speaking abuse against him
decisions.reason: The verb means to slander or insult. Mark's readers would also hear in it the charge of blasphemy brought against Jesus (14:64), now turned on those who mock him.

decisions.choice: shaking their heads: Psalm 22:8
decisions.reason: The psalm says: all who see me mock me; they shake their heads. In Lamentations 2:15 passers-by wag their heads at Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: destroying the temple and building it in three days: the charge at the hearing
decisions.reason: False witnesses claimed Jesus said he would destroy the temple and build another in three days (14:58). Mark has not recorded such a saying from Jesus, though he foretold the temple's fall (13:2).

decisions.choice: Aha: a cry of scorn
decisions.reason: The word mocks someone in his downfall.

decisions.choice: save yourself: the mockers' demand, which Jesus refuses
decisions.reason: Jesus had said that whoever wants to save his life will lose it (8:35). He does not come down.

decisions.choice: the taunt split into exclamations
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long taunt into shorter cries. Readable says "You said you would" for the participles.

decisions.choice: yourself
decisions.reason: The mockers speak to Jesus, so the pronoun for him is written as a pronoun for Christ.

decisions.choice: the mockers address Jesus as "ông" and say "tự cứu mình", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Opponents speak to Jesus as "ông" (as in John). The reflexive "mình" is not a pronoun of respect, so the English span on "yourself" has no counterpart. "mày" would be cruder than the Greek.

decisions.choice: The mockers speak to and about Jesus with no honorific ("너", "자", "그"), here and in 15:31-32 and 15:35-36
decisions.reason: The speakers are hostile; giving him honorifics in their mouths would misrepresent what they say (as in Mark 3:22 and John 11:48). The narrator still honours him.

decisions.choice: "모독하다" (L); "욕설을 퍼붓다" (B); "욕을 하다" (R) for blasphemeo
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word used of blasphemy in Mark 3:28-29, since the abuse is aimed at God's Son; Balanced and Readable say what the passers-by did.

decisions.choice: lo insultaban (L); lo cubrían de insultos (B); le gritaba insultos (R)
decisions.reason: The verb here means speaking abuse against him (meaning decision m1); in Spanish "blasfemar" now suggests only speech against God, so every level says "insultar".

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}; a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo
decisions.reason: The stressed pronouns addressed to Jesus take the deity_pronoun setting; the clitic in "sálvate" and "mírate" does not. As in English, Balanced and Readable split the taunt into exclamations.

decisions.choice: blasphémaient contre lui (L); l'insultaient (B); lançaient des insultes (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is the one used for speaking against God; here it is abuse against Jesus (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "blasphémer" so the reader sees the word Mark chose; Balanced and Readable say what the passers-by were doing.

decisions.choice: sauve-toi, with the span on "toi"
decisions.reason: French says "save yourself" with the reflexive "sauve-toi", so the span goes on that "toi" where the English has it on "yourself"; adding "toi-même" only to carry it would be heavy.

decisions.choice: kumtukana (abuse him)
decisions.reason: The verb here is abuse spoken against a man (meaning decision). "Kukufuru" in Swahili is speaking against God, which would say more than the passers-by mean, so every level says "kumtukana".

decisions.choice: jiokoe {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}; "Wewe" plain at the start of a sentence
decisions.reason: The reflexive "-ji-" is inside the verb, so the reader setting goes on "mwenyewe" (yourself). Where "Wewe" opens a sentence it is capitalised either way and is written plainly, as the style guide says.

source.text: ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων ἔλεγον· Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι·

records.literal_gloss: Likewise also the chief priests mocking to one another with the scribes were saying, Others he saved, himself not he is able to save.

en.L: Likewise the chief priests also, mocking [him] to one another with the scribes, were saying, "Others {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved; {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot save.
en.B: The chief priests and the scribes mocked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the same way among themselves. "He saved other people," they said, "but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot save {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}!
en.R: The leading priests and the teachers of God's law also made fun of Jesus. They said to each other, "He saved other people, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot save {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}!

vi.L: Cũng vậy, các thầy tế lễ cả cùng với các thầy thông giáo chế nhạo [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] với nhau mà nói: "Ông ta đã cứu những người khác, còn chính mình thì không cứu được.
vi.B: Các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo cũng chế nhạo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như thế với nhau: "Ông ta cứu được người khác, mà chẳng cứu nổi chính mình!
vi.R: Các thầy tế lễ đứng đầu và các thầy dạy luật cũng chế giễu Đức Giê-xu. Họ nói với nhau: "Ông ta đã cứu người khác, nhưng lại không cứu được chính mình!

ko.L: 마찬가지로 대제사장들도 율법학자들과 함께 서로 [그분을] 조롱하며 말하고 있었다. "그가 남들은 구원했으나, 자기 자신은 구원하지 못한다.
ko.B: 대제사장들과 율법학자들도 마찬가지로 자기들끼리 예수를 조롱하며 말했다. "남들은 구원하더니, 자기 자신은 구원하지 못하는군!
ko.R: 대제사장들과 율법을 가르치는 선생들도 예수를 놀려 댔다. 그들은 서로 말했다. "다른 사람들은 구해 주더니, 자기 자신은 구하지 못하는군!

es.L: De igual manera también los principales sacerdotes, burlándose entre ellos con los escribas, decían: «A otros salvó; a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo no puede salvar.
es.B: Del mismo modo, los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas se burlaban de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entre ellos. «Salvó a otros», decían, «¡pero a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo no se puede salvar!
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley también se burlaban de Jesús. Se decían unos a otros: «Salvó a otros, pero no puede salvarse a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo.

fr.L: De même aussi les chefs des prêtres, se moquant [de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}] entre eux avec les scribes, disaient : « D’autres, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [les] a sauvés ; {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne peut pas se sauver.
fr.B: De la même façon, les chefs des prêtres et les scribes se moquaient de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} entre eux : « Il a sauvé les autres, disaient-ils, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne peut pas se sauver {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} !
fr.R: Les chefs des prêtres et les spécialistes de la Loi se moquaient aussi de Jésus. Ils se disaient entre eux : « Il a sauvé les autres, mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne peut pas se sauver {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} !

sw.L: Vivyo hivyo wakuu wa makuhani pia, wakimdhihaki wao kwa wao pamoja na waandishi, walikuwa wakisema, "Wengine aliwaokoa; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} hawezi kujiokoa.
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi nao walimdhihaki vivyo hivyo wao kwa wao. "Aliwaokoa wengine," walisema, "lakini hawezi kujiokoa {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}!
sw.R: Viongozi wa makuhani na walimu wa Sheria nao walimfanyia Yesu mzaha. Waliambiana, "Aliwaokoa watu wengine, lakini hawezi kujiokoa {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}!

decisions.choice: saved: rescued, and also healed
decisions.reason: The verb is used for Jesus' healings (5:34; 6:56; 10:52). The leaders admit that he rescued others.

decisions.choice: he cannot save himself: what they mean as scorn is true in another sense
decisions.reason: The leaders say he has no power. Mark's readers know he would not save himself, because he came to give his life (10:45).

decisions.choice: to one another: among themselves
decisions.reason: The leaders talk about Jesus to each other, not to him.

decisions.choice: himself
decisions.reason: The leaders speak of Jesus, so the pronouns for him take the setting for pronouns for Christ.

decisions.choice: "Ông ta ... chính mình" with no deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The leaders speak of Jesus as "ông ta", and "mình" is a plain reflexive; neither has a reverent capital form.

decisions.choice: "구원하다" (L, B); "구하다" (R) for sozo, here and in 15:30
decisions.reason: Their scorn says more than they mean (meaning decision); "구원하다" keeps the word of salvation, and Readable's "구하다" (rescue) is still the same Korean root.

decisions.choice: salvó ... salvar; a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "salvar" twice, so the scorn that is true in another sense can be heard (meaning decisions m1, m2). The stressed "sí mismo" for Christ takes the setting.

decisions.choice: sauver ... se sauver (every level)
decisions.reason: One French verb at every level keeps the irony the meaning decisions describe: "sauver" covers the rescues and healings the scoffers have in mind, and what they say in scorn is true in another sense (meaning decisions m1 and m2).

decisions.choice: Wengine aliwaokoa; yeye mwenyewe hawezi kujiokoa (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, with "others" and "himself" set at the head of each clause, so the contrast the mockers draw (meaning decision) is heard. Swahili needs the free pronouns "yeye mwenyewe" to stress "himself", so they are not bracketed.

source.text: ὁ χριστὸς ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ, ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ πιστεύσωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: The Christ, the King of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, that we may see and believe.

en.L: Let the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe."
en.B: Let {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the King of Israel, come down from the cross right now, so that we can see it and believe!"
en.R: This man says he is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the King of Israel. Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} come down from the cross now! When we see that, we will believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

vi.L: Hãy để {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, Vua của Y-sơ-ra-ên, bây giờ xuống khỏi cây thập tự, để chúng ta thấy và tin."
vi.B: Hãy để {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, Vua của Y-sơ-ra-ên, xuống khỏi cây thập tự ngay bây giờ, để chúng ta thấy mà tin!"
vi.R: Người này tự xưng là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, Vua của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Hãy để ông ta xuống khỏi cây thập tự ngay bây giờ đi! Khi thấy điều đó, chúng ta sẽ tin ông ta."

ko.L: 우리가 보고 믿도록, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}, 이스라엘의 왕은 지금 십자가에서 내려오라."
ko.B: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}, 이스라엘의 왕이 지금 당장 십자가에서 내려와 보라지! 그러면 우리가 보고 믿겠다!"
ko.R: 이 사람은 자기가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}이고 이스라엘의 왕이라고 했다. 그렇다면 지금 십자가에서 내려와 보라지! 그것을 보면 우리도 그를 믿겠다."

es.L: ¡Que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Rey de Israel, baje ahora de la cruz, para que veamos y creamos!».
es.B: ¡Que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Rey de Israel, baje ahora mismo de la cruz, para que lo veamos y creamos!».
es.R: Este dice que es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Rey de Israel. ¡Que baje ahora de la cruz! Cuando lo veamos, creeremos en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».

fr.L: Le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le roi d’Israël, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} descende maintenant de la croix, afin que nous voyions et que nous croyions ! »
fr.B: Que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le roi d’Israël, descende maintenant de la croix, pour que nous voyions et que nous croyions ! »
fr.R: Cet homme dit qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le roi d’Israël. Qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} descende de la croix maintenant ! Quand nous verrons cela, nous croirons en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »

sw.L: Yule {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mfalme wa Israeli, na ashuke sasa kutoka msalabani, ili tuone na kuamini."
sw.B: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mfalme wa Israeli, na ashuke kutoka msalabani sasa hivi, ili tuone, tupate kuamini!"
sw.R: Mtu huyu anasema {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mfalme wa Israeli. Basi na ashuke kutoka msalabani sasa! Tukiona hivyo, tutamwamini."

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, God's anointed king
decisions.reason: The leaders use the title the high priest asked about (14:61). They mean it as scorn.

decisions.choice: the King of Israel: the title said by Jews
decisions.reason: Pilate and the soldiers said "King of the Jews", the way outsiders spoke. The leaders say "King of Israel", Israel's own name for itself.

decisions.choice: that we may see and believe: they demand a sign
decisions.reason: They ask for proof on their own terms, as the Pharisees asked for a sign in 8:11-12. Jesus refused then and does not answer now.

decisions.choice: This man says he is
alternatives: the Christ, the King of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the leaders are repeating the claim with scorn.

decisions.choice: believe in him
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they would believe. Mark leaves it unstated; it may mean believe in him or believe the claim.

decisions.choice: inclusive "chúng ta"
decisions.reason: The leaders are speaking among themselves (15:31), so "we" includes the hearers.

decisions.choice: "ông ta" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: In the mockers' mouth Jesus is "ông ta", which has no capital form.

decisions.choice: {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} at every level; a mocking third-person command, "내려오라" (L), "내려와 보라지" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The christos span of the style guide, section 7; both forms end in a vowel, so the particles after the span fit both. Korean has no third-person imperative; the written "-라" (L) and the scornful "-라지" (B, R) carry the taunt.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} at every level
decisions.reason: As in John Spanish (1:25), "Cristo" here is a title, so it keeps the article, with "Mesías" as the reader's alternative (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Este dice que es; creeremos en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable shows that the title is the mockers' scorn and says whom they would believe (meaning decisions m2, m3).

decisions.choice: Le Christ, le roi d'Israël, qu'il descende (L)
alternatives: Que le Christ, le roi d'Israël, descende (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, with the titles first and the command after, as a taunt shouted at the cross; Balanced uses the ordinary French order.

decisions.choice: Yule {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek has the article: "the Christ", the title (meaning decision). Swahili has no article, so Literal marks it with "yule" (that one, the one spoken of), as the English Literal writes "the". Balanced and Readable use the title alone.

source.text: καὶ οἱ συνεσταυρωμένοι σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And those crucified with him were insulting him.

en.L: And those crucified with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were insulting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Even the men crucified with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} heaped insults on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The two men on the crosses next to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} also insulted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Và những người bị đóng đinh cùng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sỉ nhục {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ngay cả những kẻ bị đóng đinh với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng buông lời nhục mạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Hai người bị đóng đinh hai bên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng sỉ nhục {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그분과 함께 십자가에 못 박힌 사람들도 그분을 욕하고 있었다.
ko.B: 예수와 함께 십자가에 못 박힌 사람들까지도 예수를 모욕했다.
ko.R: 예수 곁에서 십자가에 달린 두 사람도 예수를 욕했다.

es.L: Y los que estaban crucificados con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} lo insultaban.
es.B: Hasta los que estaban crucificados con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} lo llenaban de insultos.
es.R: Los dos hombres que estaban en las cruces junto a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} también lo insultaban.

fr.L: Et ceux qui avaient été crucifiés avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}insultaient.
fr.B: Même les hommes crucifiés avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accablaient d’insultes.
fr.R: Les deux hommes cloués sur les croix à côté de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}insultaient aussi.

sw.L: Na wale waliosulubiwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} walikuwa wakimsuta.
sw.B: Hata wale waliosulubiwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} walimsuta pia.
sw.R: Wale watu wawili waliopigiliwa misumari kwenye misalaba karibu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} nao walimtukana.

decisions.choice: were insulting: taunting, reproaching
decisions.reason: The verb means to heap scorn on someone.

decisions.choice: all mock him: passers-by, leaders and fellow victims
decisions.reason: Mark lists three groups who mock him, so that Jesus is left completely alone. Psalm 69:10 speaks of the insults of those who insult God falling on his servant.

decisions.choice: the two men on the crosses next to him
decisions.reason: Readable points back to the two of 15:27.

decisions.choice: Los dos hombres que estaban en las cruces (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says who these were, the two men of 15:27.

source.text: Καὶ γενομένης ὥρας ἕκτης σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης.

records.literal_gloss: And having come [the] hour sixth darkness came over all the land until [the] hour ninth.

en.L: And when the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
en.B: At noon darkness fell over the whole land and lasted until three in the afternoon.
en.R: At twelve o'clock noon, the whole land became dark. It stayed dark until three o'clock in the afternoon.

vi.L: Và khi đến giờ thứ sáu, bóng tối bao trùm khắp cả xứ cho đến giờ thứ chín.
vi.B: Đến giữa trưa, bóng tối bao phủ khắp xứ cho đến ba giờ chiều.
vi.R: Lúc mười hai giờ trưa, cả xứ trở nên tối tăm. Trời tối như vậy cho đến ba giờ chiều.

ko.L: 그리고 여섯째 시가 되자, 온 땅에 어둠이 내려 아홉째 시까지 계속되었다.
ko.B: 낮 열두 시가 되자 온 땅이 어둠에 덮였고, 그 어둠은 오후 세 시까지 계속되었다.
ko.R: 낮 열두 시가 되자 온 땅이 캄캄해졌다. 오후 세 시까지 계속 어두웠다.

es.L: Y llegada la hora sexta, hubo oscuridad sobre toda la tierra hasta la hora novena.
es.B: Al mediodía, la oscuridad cubrió toda la tierra hasta las tres de la tarde.
es.R: A las doce del día, toda la tierra quedó a oscuras. Siguió oscuro hasta las tres de la tarde.

fr.L: Et la sixième heure étant venue, il y eut des ténèbres sur tout le pays jusqu’à la neuvième heure.
fr.B: À midi, l’obscurité se fit sur tout le pays, et elle dura jusqu’à quinze heures.
fr.R: À midi, tout le pays est devenu sombre. L’obscurité a duré jusqu’à trois heures de l’après-midi.

sw.L: Na ilipofika saa sita, giza likaja juu ya nchi yote mpaka saa tisa.
sw.B: Ilipofika saa sita, giza liliifunika nchi yote mpaka saa tisa.
sw.R: Ilipofika saa sita mchana, nchi yote ikawa giza. Giza lilidumu mpaka saa tisa alasiri.

decisions.choice: the sixth hour, the ninth hour: about noon and about three in the afternoon
alternatives: six and nine in the morning
decisions.reason: The hours were counted from sunrise, as in 15:25.

decisions.choice: the whole land: the land of Israel, or the whole earth
decisions.reason: The same word can mean land or earth. Mark does not say how far the darkness reached.

decisions.choice: darkness: a sign of God's judgment
decisions.reason: Amos 8:9 says that on that day God will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight. Darkness also came on Egypt before the Passover (Exodus 10:22).

decisions.choice: the darkness was not an eclipse
decisions.reason: Passover fell at full moon, when an eclipse of the sun cannot happen. Mark does not say how the darkness came.

decisions.choice: noon, three in the afternoon (B); twelve o'clock noon, three o'clock in the afternoon (R)
alternatives: the sixth hour, the ninth hour
decisions.reason: As in 15:25, Literal keeps the ancient hours and the other levels give the time as we count it.

decisions.choice: la hora sexta, la hora novena (L); mediodía, las tres de la tarde (B, R); toda la tierra (every level)
decisions.reason: Clock times as in 15:25 (meaning decision m1). Spanish "tierra" means both the land and the earth, so every level keeps the question of meaning decision m2 open.

decisions.choice: tout le pays (every level)
decisions.reason: French "toute la terre" is read as the whole earth, while "tout le pays", like the English "the whole land", is read first as the land of Israel; the meaning decision m2 gives both senses. Literal says "ténèbres", the word for darkness as a sign (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable use the plainer "obscurité".

source.text: καὶ τῇ ἐνάτῃ ὥρᾳ ἐβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Ἐλωῒ ἐλωῒ λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι;

records.literal_gloss: And at the ninth hour cried out Jesus with a voice loud, Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?

en.L: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"
en.B: At three o'clock Jesus gave a loud shout: "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"
en.R: At three o'clock Jesus shouted loudly, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"

vi.L: Và vào giờ thứ chín, Đức Giê-xu kêu lớn tiếng: "Ê-lô-i, Ê-lô-i, lê-ma sa-bách-tha-ni?"
vi.B: Lúc ba giờ chiều, Đức Giê-xu kêu lớn: "Ê-lô-i, Ê-lô-i, lê-ma sa-bách-tha-ni?"
vi.R: Lúc ba giờ chiều, Đức Giê-xu kêu thật lớn: "Ê-lô-i, Ê-lô-i, lê-ma sa-bách-tha-ni?"

ko.L: 그리고 아홉째 시에 예수께서 큰 소리로 외치셨다. "엘로이, 엘로이, 레마 사박다니?"
ko.B: 오후 세 시에 예수께서 큰 소리로 부르짖으셨다. "엘로이, 엘로이, 레마 사박다니?"
ko.R: 오후 세 시에 예수께서 큰 소리로 외치셨다. "엘로이, 엘로이, 레마 사박다니?"

es.L: Y a la hora novena Jesús gritó con gran voz: «Eloí, Eloí, ¿lemá sabactaní?».
es.B: A las tres de la tarde Jesús gritó con fuerza: «Eloí, Eloí, ¿lemá sabactaní?».
es.R: A las tres de la tarde Jesús gritó muy fuerte: «Eloí, Eloí, ¿lemá sabactaní?».

fr.L: Et à la neuvième heure, Jésus cria d’une voix forte : « Éloï, Éloï, lema sabachthani ? »
fr.B: À quinze heures, Jésus poussa un grand cri : « Éloï, Éloï, lema sabachthani ? »
fr.R: À trois heures de l’après-midi, Jésus a crié très fort : « Éloï, Éloï, lema sabachthani ? »

sw.L: Na saa tisa Yesu akalia kwa sauti kuu, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"
sw.B: Saa tisa Yesu alipaza sauti kwa nguvu, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"
sw.R: Saa tisa alasiri Yesu alilia kwa sauti kubwa, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"

decisions.choice: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani: the first line of Psalm 22, in Aramaic
decisions.reason: Jesus prays the opening of Psalm 22 (22:2 in the Hebrew numbering) in Aramaic, the everyday language of Jews in his land. The psalm moves from a cry of abandonment to praise of God who rescues (Psalm 22:23-32). Mark has already echoed the psalm in 15:24 and 15:29.

decisions.choice: the cry: Jesus' real experience of being forsaken
alternatives: only a quotation with no feeling
God had stopped being his God
decisions.reason: Jesus still calls him "my God". The cry expresses deep anguish while holding on to God. Mark does not explain it further.

decisions.choice: cried out with a loud voice: shouted aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase shows strength, not the faint voice of a dying man.

decisions.choice: Eloi ... lema sabachthani: the spelling of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Eli ... lama sabachthani (the Hebrew form in some manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The manuscripts spell these words in several ways, some closer to the Hebrew of the psalm, as in Matthew 27:46. The SBLGNT has the Aramaic form. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani
decisions.reason: All levels keep the Aramaic words as Mark does, because Mark translates them in the next sentence and the misunderstanding in 15:35 depends on their sound. Balanced and Readable give the hour as three o'clock, as in 15:33.

decisions.choice: "Ê-lô-i, Ê-lô-i, lê-ma sa-bách-tha-ni?"
decisions.reason: The Aramaic words are kept as sounds, as in the English, in the hyphenated Vietnamese way of writing foreign names, following the SBLGNT spelling ("lema").

decisions.choice: "엘로이, 엘로이, 레마 사박다니" at every level
decisions.reason: The Aramaic is written in Hangul following the spelling of the SBLGNT (meaning decision), as the English follows it; "라마" is the form familiar from older Korean Bibles.

decisions.choice: Eloí, Eloí, ¿lemá sabactaní?
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the Aramaic words as Mark gives them, spelled as Spanish reads them (meaning decisions m1, m4), as John 20:16 Spanish does with "Rabuni"; Mark's own translation follows.

decisions.choice: Éloï, Éloï, lema sabachthani (every level)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic words stay as Mark gives them, in the spelling of the SBLGNT (meaning decision m4). The accent and diaeresis on "Éloï" tell French readers to say three syllables, as the Greek marks it; without them French readers would say "Eloi" as one rhyme with "loi".

source.text: ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Ὁ θεός μου ὁ θεός μου, εἰς τί ἐγκατέλιπές με;

records.literal_gloss: Which is being translated, The God of me, the God of me, for what did you forsake me?

en.L: Which is translated, "My God, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.B: That means, "My God, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, why did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} abandon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.R: These words mean, "My God, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} all alone?"

vi.L: Dịch ra là: "Đức Chúa Trời của con, Đức Chúa Trời của con, sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lìa bỏ con?"
vi.B: Nghĩa là: "Đức Chúa Trời của con, Đức Chúa Trời của con, sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bỏ con?"
vi.R: Những lời ấy có nghĩa là: "Đức Chúa Trời của con, Đức Chúa Trời của con, sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bỏ con một mình?"

ko.L: 이것을 번역하면 "나의 하나님, 나의 하나님, 어찌하여 저를 버리셨습니까?"라는 뜻이다.
ko.B: 그것은 "나의 하나님, 나의 하나님, 왜 저를 버리셨습니까?"라는 뜻이다.
ko.R: 이 말은 "나의 하나님, 나의 하나님, 왜 저를 혼자 버려두셨습니까?"라는 뜻이다.

es.L: Que traducido es: «Dios mío, Dios mío, ¿por qué me has abandonado?».
es.B: Eso significa: «Dios mío, Dios mío, ¿por qué me abandonaste?».
es.R: Esas palabras quieren decir: «Dios mío, Dios mío, ¿por qué me has dejado solo?».

fr.L: Ce qui se traduit : « Mon Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} abandonné ? »
fr.B: Ce qui veut dire : « Mon Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} abandonné ? »
fr.R: Ces mots veulent dire : « Mon Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Dieu, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}as-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} laissé tout seul ? »

sw.L: Maana yake, ikitafsiriwa, ni, "Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, kwa nini umeniacha?"
sw.B: Maana yake ni, "Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, kwa nini umenitelekeza?"
sw.R: Maneno hayo maana yake ni, "Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, kwa nini umeniacha peke {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}?"

decisions.choice: forsaken: left behind, abandoned
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave someone in a time of need.

decisions.choice: for what: why
decisions.reason: The phrase asks why, in the words of Psalm 22:2.

decisions.choice: The God of me: my God, a form of address
decisions.reason: The article with the noun is used as a vocative, as often in Greek translated from Hebrew.

decisions.choice: left me all alone
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for forsaken. Literal keeps the traditional word.

decisions.choice: "con" for Jesus' "my" and "me", with no deity_pronoun span; God addressed as {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}
alternatives: "tôi" (as the psalm is quoted in John 19:24)
decisions.reason: Jesus prays the psalm as his own cry to God, and in prayer he calls himself "con" (as to the Father in John 17). "con" is a noun of address with no capital form, so the English span on "my/me" has no counterpart.

decisions.choice: Jesus prays to God in 합쇼체 with "저" ("버리셨습니까?")
decisions.reason: As Jesus prays to the Father in John 17 and as the psalmist speaks to God (style guide, sections 4 and 7a); this is the first line of Psalm 22.

decisions.choice: me has abandonado (L); me abandonaste (B); me has dejado solo (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave behind, to abandon (meaning decision m1); "desamparar" is the older word. The pronouns are "mío" and the clitic "me", which the Spanish deity_pronoun setting does not cover.

decisions.choice: Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} twice
decisions.reason: In English the first "My" opens the sentence and is written plainly. In Swahili the possessive follows the noun, so neither "wangu" is sentence-initial and both take the reader setting, as Jesus speaks of himself.

decisions.choice: umenitelekeza (B)
decisions.reason: "Kutelekeza" is to abandon someone who depends on you, the sense of the Greek (meaning decision), as the English Balanced says "abandon". Literal keeps the plainer "umeniacha" (you have left me), and Readable adds "peke yangu" (all alone).

source.text: καί τινες τῶν παρεστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον· Ἴδε Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: And some of those standing by, having heard, were saying, Look, Elijah he calls.

en.L: And some of those standing by, when they heard [it], were saying, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is calling Elijah!"
en.B: Some of the bystanders heard it and said, "Listen, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is calling for Elijah!"
en.R: Some of the people standing there heard this. They said, "Listen! He is calling for Elijah!"

vi.L: Và vài người trong số những người đứng đó, nghe [vậy], nói: "Kìa, ông ấy gọi Ê-li!"
vi.B: Một vài người đứng gần đó nghe vậy thì nói: "Nghe kìa, ông ấy đang gọi Ê-li!"
vi.R: Có mấy người đứng đó nghe thấy. Họ nói: "Nghe kìa! Ông ấy đang gọi Ê-li!"

ko.L: 그러자 곁에 서 있던 사람들 가운데 몇이 듣고 말했다. "보아라, 그가 엘리야를 부른다."
ko.B: 곁에 서 있던 사람들 가운데 몇 사람이 이 말을 듣고 말했다. "들어 보아라, 저 사람이 엘리야를 부른다!"
ko.R: 거기 서 있던 사람들 가운데 몇이 이 소리를 들었다. 그들이 말했다. "들어 보아라! 저 사람이 엘리야를 부르고 있다!"

es.L: Y algunos de los que estaban presentes, cuando [lo] oyeron, decían: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, llama a Elías».
es.B: Algunos de los que estaban allí lo oyeron y dijeron: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, está llamando a Elías».
es.R: Algunas de las personas que estaban allí oyeron esto y dijeron: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! ¡Está llamando a Elías!».

fr.L: Et quelques-uns de ceux qui se tenaient là, ayant entendu, disaient : « Voyez, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appelle Élie ! »
fr.B: Quelques-uns de ceux qui étaient là l’entendirent et dirent : « Écoutez, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appelle Élie ! »
fr.R: Quelques personnes qui étaient là ont entendu cela. Elles ont dit : « Écoutez ! Il appelle Élie ! »

sw.L: Na baadhi ya wale waliosimama karibu, waliposikia, walikuwa wakisema, "Tazama, anamwita Eliya!"
sw.B: Baadhi ya watu waliokuwa wamesimama pale walisikia, wakasema, "Sikilizeni, anamwita Eliya!"
sw.R: Baadhi ya watu waliokuwa wamesimama pale walisikia maneno hayo. Wakasema, "Sikilizeni! Anamwita Eliya!"

decisions.choice: Elijah: the cry sounded like Elijah's name
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "Eli" (my God) sounds close to the name Elijah. Many Jews believed Elijah would come to help the righteous in trouble, and that he would come before the end (9:11; Malachi 4:5).

decisions.choice: some of those standing by: Mark does not say who
decisions.reason: The talk about Elijah suggests Jews rather than Roman soldiers. Mark does not say whether they misheard or mocked on purpose.

decisions.choice: Look: listen, see
alternatives: a command to look at something
decisions.reason: The word draws attention, like "listen".

decisions.choice: Listen
decisions.reason: What drew attention was the cry, so Balanced and Readable use "Listen".

decisions.choice: "ông ấy" with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The bystanders speak of Jesus as an ordinary man; "ông ấy" has no capital form for the setting.

decisions.choice: Miren (L); Escuchen (B, R), with the ustedes / vosotros setting
decisions.reason: The word calls the others' attention (meaning decision m3); Spanish says it to a group in the plural, so it takes the reader setting. Balanced and Readable say "escuchen", since it is a cry they heard.

source.text: δραμὼν δέ τις καὶ γεμίσας σπόγγον ὄξους περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν, λέγων· Ἄφετε ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας καθελεῖν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Having run then someone and having filled a sponge with sour wine, having put [it] on a reed, was giving to drink him, saying, Leave, let us see if comes Elijah to take down him.

en.L: Then someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, put [it] on a reed, and was giving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a drink, saying, "Leave [him]; let us see if Elijah comes to take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down."
en.B: Someone ran and soaked a sponge in sour wine, put it on the end of a stick and offered it to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to drink. "Wait!" he said. "Let us see if Elijah will come and take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down."
en.R: One man ran and got a sponge. He filled it with cheap sour wine and put it on the end of a stick. He held it up to Jesus' mouth to drink. He said, "Wait! Let us see whether Elijah will come and take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down from the cross."

vi.L: Rồi có người chạy đến, lấy bọt biển thấm đầy rượu chua, cắm vào một cây sậy, đưa cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} uống, và nói: "Hãy để yên; chúng ta xem Ê-li có đến đem ông ấy xuống không."
vi.B: Một người chạy đi lấy bọt biển nhúng đẫm rượu chua, gắn vào đầu một cây gậy và đưa lên cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} uống. Người ấy nói: "Khoan đã! Để xem Ê-li có đến đem ông ấy xuống không."
vi.R: Một người chạy đi lấy một miếng bọt biển. Người ấy nhúng nó vào rượu chua rẻ tiền rồi gắn vào đầu một cây gậy. Người ấy đưa lên miệng Đức Giê-xu cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} uống. Người ấy nói: "Khoan đã! Chúng ta hãy xem Ê-li có đến đem ông ấy xuống khỏi cây thập tự không."

ko.L: 그러자 어떤 사람이 달려가서 해면에 신 포도주를 적셔 갈대에 꽂아 그분께 마시게 하며 말했다. "내버려 두어라. 엘리야가 와서 그를 내려 주는지 보자."
ko.B: 어떤 사람이 달려가서 해면을 신 포도주에 적셔 갈대 막대기 끝에 꽂아 예수께 마시게 하며 말했다. "가만있어라! 엘리야가 와서 그를 내려 주나 보자."
ko.R: 어떤 사람이 달려가서 스펀지를 가져왔다. 그리고 그것을 값싼 신 포도주에 적셔서 막대기 끝에 꽂았다. 그리고 그것을 예수의 입에 대고 마시게 했다. 그 사람이 말했다. "기다려 보아라! 엘리야가 와서 그를 십자가에서 내려 주는지 보자."

es.L: Entonces uno corrió, llenó una esponja de vino agrio, [la] puso en una caña y le daba de beber, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}}, veamos si viene Elías a bajarlo».
es.B: Uno de ellos corrió, empapó una esponja en vino agrio, la puso en la punta de una vara y se la ofreció para que bebiera. «¡{{plural_you:Esperen|Esperad}}!», dijo. «Veamos si viene Elías a bajarlo».
es.R: Un hombre fue corriendo a buscar una esponja. La empapó en vino agrio barato y la puso en la punta de una vara. La acercó a la boca de Jesús para que bebiera. Y dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Esperen|Esperad}}! Vamos a ver si Elías viene a bajarlo de la cruz».

fr.L: Alors quelqu’un courut, remplit une éponge de vin aigre, [la] mit au bout d’un roseau et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} donnait à boire, en disant : « Laissez ! Voyons si Élie vient {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} descendre. »
fr.B: Quelqu’un courut tremper une éponge dans du vin aigre, la fixa au bout d’un bâton et la {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} tendit pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} boive. « Attendez ! dit-il. Voyons si Élie va venir {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} descendre de là. »
fr.R: Un homme a couru chercher une éponge. Il l’a remplie de vin aigre bon marché et il l’a mise au bout d’un bâton. Il l’a levée jusqu’à la bouche de Jésus pour qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} boive. Il a dit : « Attendez ! Voyons si Élie va venir {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} descendre de la croix. »

sw.L: Basi mtu mmoja akakimbia, akajaza sifongo divai chungu, akaiweka juu ya mwanzi, akawa akimnywesha, akisema, "Acheni, tuone kama Eliya anakuja kumshusha."
sw.B: Mtu mmoja akakimbia, akachovya sifongo katika divai chungu, akaiweka kwenye ncha ya fimbo, akampa anywe. Akasema, "Ngojeni! Tuone kama Eliya atakuja kumshusha."
sw.R: Mtu mmoja alikimbia akaleta sifongo. Akaijaza divai chungu ya bei nafuu, akaiweka kwenye ncha ya fimbo. Akaiinua mpaka kinywani mwa Yesu ili anywe. Akasema, "Ngojeni! Tuone kama Eliya atakuja kumshusha kutoka msalabani."

decisions.choice: sour wine: cheap wine gone sour, a common drink
decisions.reason: Soldiers and laborers drank this sharp wine mixed with water. It quenched thirst.

decisions.choice: sour wine to drink: Psalm 69:22
decisions.reason: The psalm says: for my thirst they gave me sour wine to drink.

decisions.choice: Leave: wait, let him be
alternatives: let him alone with no drink
decisions.reason: The word means let go or allow. Here it means hold off, wait and see. It can also be read as "let me" give him the drink.

decisions.choice: giving him a drink while mocking: whether kind or cruel is not clear
decisions.reason: The drink may have been meant to keep Jesus alive a little longer to see if Elijah came. The words sound like scorn. Mark does not say what the man meant.

decisions.choice: cheap; from the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of wine it was and where Jesus would be taken down from.

decisions.choice: "rượu chua"
