decisions.reason: As in John 19:29: "giấm" today means cooking vinegar; "rượu chua" is the soured wine the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "신 포도주" at every level; "해면" (L, B), "스펀지" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean John 19:29; "초" (vinegar) in older versions misleads, since it was cheap wine gone sour.

decisions.choice: vino agrio (every level); caña (L); vara (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in John 19:29 Spanish: "vinagre" today means something no one drinks, while "vino agrio" says what it was (meaning decision m1). "Caña" and "vara" as in 15:19.

decisions.choice: Dejen (L); Esperen (B, R), with the ustedes / vosotros setting
decisions.reason: The command is plural in Greek, spoken to the bystanders (meaning decision m3), so it takes the reader setting.

decisions.choice: vin aigre (every level)
decisions.reason: As in John 19:29: "vinaigre" today means something no one drinks, while "vin aigre" says what it was, the cheap sour wine people drank (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: divai chungu at every level
decisions.reason: As in Swahili John 19:29: the word means cheap wine gone sour, a common drink (meaning decision); "siki" (vinegar) is something no one drinks.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀφεὶς φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐξέπνευσεν.

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus having let go a cry loud breathed his last.

en.L: But Jesus, letting out a loud cry, breathed [his] last.
en.B: But Jesus gave a loud cry and breathed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} last.
en.R: Then Jesus cried out loudly, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died.

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu, kêu lên một tiếng lớn, tắt thở.
vi.B: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu kêu lên một tiếng lớn rồi tắt thở.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu kêu lên thật lớn, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chết.

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서는 큰 소리를 지르시고 숨을 거두셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 큰 소리를 지르시고 숨을 거두셨다.
ko.R: 그때 예수께서 큰 소리로 외치시고 돌아가셨다.

es.L: Pero Jesús, dando un fuerte grito, expiró.
es.B: Pero Jesús dio un fuerte grito y exhaló el último aliento.
es.R: Entonces Jesús gritó muy fuerte y murió.

fr.L: Mais Jésus, ayant poussé un grand cri, expira.
fr.B: Mais Jésus poussa un grand cri et rendit le dernier soupir.
fr.R: Puis Jésus a poussé un grand cri, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu, akitoa sauti kuu, akatoa pumzi ya mwisho.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu alilia kwa sauti kuu, akatoa pumzi ya mwisho.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alilia kwa sauti kubwa, akafa.

decisions.choice: breathed his last: died, gave up his breath
decisions.reason: The verb means to breathe out, a plain way of saying he died. It may also recall the Spirit who came into Jesus at his baptism (1:10), but the word itself means only to die.

decisions.choice: letting out a loud cry: a second loud cry, or the same cry as in 15:34
decisions.reason: Mark does not give the words of this cry. It is most likely a second cry at the moment of death.

decisions.choice: cry: a loud sound or shout
decisions.reason: The noun means a sound or a voice. Here it is a cry without words.

decisions.choice: he died
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word.

decisions.choice: "숨을 거두다" (L, B); "돌아가시다" (R) for ekpneo, here and in 15:39 and 15:44
decisions.reason: "숨을 거두다" keeps the picture of breathing one's last; Readable uses the plain honorific verb for dying, as the Korean John 19:33 Readable does.

decisions.choice: expiró (L); exhaló el último aliento (B); murió (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to breathe one's last, to die (meaning decision m1); it is not the phrase of John 19:30. Readable says it plainly. The same verb in 15:39 is "expirar" at Literal.

decisions.choice: expira (L); rendit le dernier soupir (B), and the same in 15:39
decisions.reason: Both French expressions keep the Greek picture of breathing out one's last breath (meaning decision m1), and each level repeats its wording in 15:39, where the centurion sees how he breathed his last; Readable says plainly that he died, as the English does.

decisions.choice: akatoa pumzi ya mwisho (L, B); akafa (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is "breathe out" (meaning decision). "Kutoa pumzi ya mwisho" (to give out the last breath) keeps that picture, and the same words are used in 15:39; "kukata roho" is the everyday idiom for dying but loses the breath. Swahili needs no word for "his", so Literal brackets nothing.

source.text: καὶ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη εἰς δύο ἀπ’ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω.

records.literal_gloss: And the curtain of the sanctuary was torn into two from top to bottom.

en.L: And the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom.
en.B: And the curtain in the sanctuary was split in two from top to bottom.
en.R: At that moment the curtain in the temple was torn in two pieces, from the top all the way down to the bottom.

vi.L: Và bức màn của đền thờ bị xé làm đôi từ trên xuống dưới.
vi.B: Bức màn trong đền thờ bị xé ra làm hai, từ trên xuống dưới.
vi.R: Ngay lúc ấy, bức màn trong đền thờ bị xé làm hai mảnh, từ trên xuống tận dưới.

ko.L: 그리고 성소의 휘장이 위에서부터 아래까지 두 갈래로 찢어졌다.
ko.B: 그리고 성소의 휘장이 위에서 아래까지 둘로 찢어졌다.
ko.R: 바로 그때 성전 안에 드리워져 있던 휘장이 위에서부터 아래까지 두 쪽으로 찢어졌다.

es.L: Y el velo del santuario fue rasgado en dos, de arriba abajo.
es.B: Y la cortina del santuario se rasgó en dos, de arriba abajo.
es.R: En ese momento, la cortina del templo se rasgó en dos pedazos, de arriba hasta abajo.

fr.L: Et le rideau du sanctuaire fut déchiré en deux, du haut jusqu’en bas.
fr.B: Et le rideau du sanctuaire fut déchiré en deux, de haut en bas.
fr.R: Au même moment, le rideau dans le temple a été déchiré en deux, du haut jusqu’en bas.

sw.L: Na pazia la patakatifu likapasuka vipande viwili, kutoka juu hadi chini.
sw.B: Na pazia la patakatifu pa hekalu likapasuka vipande viwili, kutoka juu mpaka chini.
sw.R: Wakati huo huo pazia la hekalu lilipasuka vipande viwili, kuanzia juu kabisa mpaka chini.

decisions.choice: was torn: ripped apart, the same verb as at Jesus' baptism
decisions.reason: Mark uses this verb only here and at 1:10, where the heavens were torn open. At the start and the end of Jesus' work, God tears something open.

decisions.choice: was torn: a passive, God is the one who tore it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, and "from top to bottom" shows the tear came from above.

decisions.choice: the curtain of the sanctuary: most likely the inner curtain before the Most Holy Place
alternatives: the outer curtain at the entrance to the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The sanctuary had two great curtains. The inner one closed off the Most Holy Place, where only the high priest went once a year (Exodus 26:31-33; Hebrews 10:19-20). The outer one hung at the entrance and could be seen from outside. Mark does not say which.

decisions.choice: the torn curtain: a sign of God's action at Jesus' death
decisions.reason: Mark does not explain it. It may show that the way to God is open, or announce judgment on the temple, which Jesus foretold (13:2). Both may be in view.

decisions.choice: sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word means the sanctuary building itself, not the whole temple area. Readable says "the temple".

decisions.choice: "đền thờ" for the sanctuary (naos)
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "đền thờ" for naos at every level (John 2:19-21); the curtain itself shows the inner sanctuary is meant, and the meaning decision and its footnote say which curtain.

decisions.choice: "성소의 휘장" (L, B); "성전 안에 드리워져 있던 휘장" (R)
decisions.reason: naos is the sanctuary itself, not the whole temple area (meaning decision), as the English Literal and Balanced; "휘장" is the ordinary word for a hanging curtain and is kept at Readable.

decisions.choice: el velo del santuario, fue rasgado (L); la cortina del santuario (B); la cortina del templo (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the passive, which leaves God as the one who tore it (meaning decision m2). "Cortina" is the everyday word for a hanging curtain; "santuario" names the inner building (meaning decision m3), and Readable says "templo", as the English does.

decisions.choice: le rideau (every level); fut déchiré, a passive (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Le voile du temple" is the familiar church phrase, but "voile" today suggests a veil worn over the face; "rideau" says what it was, a great hanging curtain (meaning decision m3). The passive is kept, not "se déchira", because God is the one who tore it (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: pazia la patakatifu (L), pazia la patakatifu pa hekalu (B), pazia la hekalu (R); kupasuka
decisions.reason: The word is the sanctuary, not the whole temple area (meaning decision), so Literal and Balanced say "patakatifu" (the holy place), Balanced adding "pa hekalu" so readers know where it is; Readable says "hekalu". "Kupasuka" (to split, be torn open) is used at every level; the tearing of the heavens at Jesus' baptism (1:10) should use the same verb, so the link the meaning decision notes is kept.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ κεντυρίων ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐξ ἐναντίας αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὕτως ἐξέπνευσεν εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος υἱὸς θεοῦ ἦν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the centurion standing by from opposite him that thus he breathed his last, he said, Truly this the man God's Son was.

en.L: And when the centurion who stood by facing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} breathed [his] last in this way, he said, "Truly this man was God's Son!"
en.B: The centurion standing in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died, and he said, "This man really was God's Son!"
en.R: A Roman army officer was standing in front of Jesus. When he saw how Jesus died, he said, "This man really was God's Son!"

vi.L: Và viên đội trưởng đứng đối diện {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tắt thở như vậy, thì nói: "Thật, người này đã là Con Đức Chúa Trời!"
vi.B: Viên đội trưởng đứng đối diện {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chết như vậy thì nói: "Người này thật là Con Đức Chúa Trời!"
vi.R: Có một sĩ quan La Mã đứng trước mặt Đức Giê-xu. Khi thấy Đức Giê-xu chết như thế, ông nói: "Người này đúng thật là Con Đức Chúa Trời!"

ko.L: 그런데 그분 맞은편에 서 있던 백부장이, 그분이 이렇게 숨을 거두시는 것을 보고 말했다. "참으로 이 사람은 하나님의 아들이었다!"
ko.B: 예수를 마주 보고 서 있던 백부장이, 예수께서 이렇게 숨을 거두시는 것을 보고 말했다. "이분은 참으로 하나님의 아들이셨다!"
ko.R: 로마 군대의 장교 한 사람이 예수 앞에 서 있었다. 그는 예수께서 어떻게 돌아가시는지 보고 말했다. "이분은 정말 하나님의 아들이셨다!"

es.L: Y el centurión que estaba de pie frente a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, al ver que había expirado de esa manera, dijo: «¡Verdaderamente este hombre era Hijo de Dios!».
es.B: El centurión que estaba frente a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} vio cómo había muerto y dijo: «¡De verdad este hombre era Hijo de Dios!».
es.R: Un oficial del ejército romano estaba de pie frente a Jesús. Cuando vio cómo había muerto Jesús, dijo: «¡De verdad este hombre era Hijo de Dios!».

fr.L: Et le centurion qui se tenait en face de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, voyant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait expiré de cette manière, dit : « Vraiment, cet homme était Fils de Dieu ! »
fr.B: Le centurion qui se tenait face à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} vit comment {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait rendu le dernier soupir et dit : « Cet homme était vraiment Fils de Dieu ! »
fr.R: Un officier de l’armée romaine se tenait en face de Jésus. Quand il a vu comment Jésus était mort, il a dit : « Cet homme était vraiment Fils de Dieu ! »

sw.L: Na yule kamanda wa askari mia, aliyesimama mkabala {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, alipoona kwamba alitoa pumzi ya mwisho hivyo, alisema, "Kweli mtu huyu alikuwa Mwana wa Mungu!"
sw.B: Kamanda wa askari mia aliyekuwa amesimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} alipoona jinsi alivyokufa, alisema, "Kwa kweli mtu huyu alikuwa Mwana wa Mungu!"
sw.R: Ofisa mmoja wa jeshi la Kirumi alikuwa amesimama mbele ya Yesu. Alipoona jinsi Yesu alivyokufa, alisema, "Kweli kabisa, mtu huyu alikuwa Mwana wa Mungu!"

decisions.choice: God's Son: the Son of God, the title Mark gives Jesus
alternatives: a son of God, a divine or godlike man in the centurion's own Roman sense
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article, so it could mean "a son of God". But a title placed before the verb often lacks the article and is still definite, and Mark began his book with Jesus as God's Son (1:1). God called him "my Son" (1:11; 9:7). For Mark, the first human to say it is a Gentile soldier at the cross. What the centurion himself understood is less certain.

decisions.choice: that he breathed his last in this way: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: that he cried out in this way and breathed his last
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "cried out and". The SBLGNT reads the shorter text. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: centurion: a Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: Mark uses the Latin title. He was in charge of the execution.

decisions.choice: was: the centurion speaks of Jesus as now dead
alternatives: he was so only in the past
decisions.reason: The past tense fits a man speaking of one who has just died.

decisions.choice: God's Son
decisions.reason: All levels say "God's Son", which keeps the same openness as the Greek and does not settle the question that the meaning decision leaves open. Readable says "a Roman army officer" for centurion.

decisions.choice: "viên đội trưởng" (L, B); "một sĩ quan La Mã" (R)
decisions.reason: "thầy đội" is the older Protestant word and now sounds dated; "viên bách quản" is a Sino-Vietnamese calque few readers know. "đội trưởng" names an officer over a unit; the meaning decision gives the size. Readable says plainly that he was a Roman officer.

decisions.choice: "백부장" (L, B); "로마 군대의 장교" (R)
decisions.reason: "백부장" is the established Korean word for a centurion; Readable says who he was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "이 사람은 ... 이었다" (L); "이분은 ... 이셨다" (B, R)
alternatives: "이 사람" with no honorific at every level
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "this man"; in Balanced and Readable the centurion's confession of who Jesus is would sound grudging in Korean without the honorific. A reviewer may prefer to keep the soldier's plain words.

decisions.choice: era Hijo de Dios, without the article
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article (meaning decision m1). Spanish "era Hijo de Dios" can carry the full title, which Mark gives Jesus, without adding "el"; the footnote gives the alternatives.

decisions.choice: un oficial del ejército romano (R); centurión (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what a centurion was (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Fils de Dieu, without an article, with a capital F (every level)
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article. "Était Fils de Dieu" keeps that, as the English "God's Son" does, while "le Fils de Dieu" would add an article and "un fils de Dieu" would make the title one of many. The capital follows the meaning decision m1 that this is the title Mark gives Jesus (1:1); the footnote there gives the other reading.

decisions.choice: kamanda wa askari mia (L, B); ofisa wa jeshi la Kirumi (R); also 15:44-45
decisions.reason: A Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers (meaning decision). "Kamanda wa askari mia" (commander of a hundred soldiers) says what he was in plain modern words, matching "kamanda" for the tribune in Swahili John 18:12; "akida" and "jemadari" are older titles that many readers would not place. Readable says "a Roman army officer", as the English does.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Mungu, at every level
decisions.reason: The English says "God's Son" to leave open whether the Greek, without the article, means "the Son of God" (meaning decision). Swahili has no article, so "Mwana wa Mungu" already leaves the same question open; it keeps the capital, as the title Mark gives Jesus (1:1).

source.text: Ἦσαν δὲ καὶ γυναῖκες ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι, ἐν αἷς καὶ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου τοῦ μικροῦ καὶ Ἰωσῆτος μήτηρ καὶ Σαλώμη, αἳ ὅτε ἦν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἄλλαι πολλαὶ αἱ συναναβᾶσαι αὐτῷ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

records.literal_gloss: Now there were also women from afar watching, among whom also Mary the Magdalene and Mary the of James the small and of Joses mother and Salome, \v 41 who, when he was in Galilee, were following him and serving him, and other many who came up with him to Jerusalem.

en.L: Now there were also women watching from a distance, among whom [were] also Mary the Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome, \v 41 who, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in Galilee, used to follow {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and many other [women] who had come up with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to Jerusalem.
en.B: Women were also there, looking on from far off, among them Mary Magdalene; Mary, mother of the younger James and of Joses; and Salome. \v 41 In Galilee they had followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and looked after {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} needs. Many other women were there as well, who had come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up to Jerusalem.
en.R: Some women were watching from far away. Mary from the town of Magdala was there. So was another Mary, the mother of the younger James and of Joses. Salome was there too. \v 41 These women had followed Jesus in Galilee and had taken care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Many other women were there also. They had come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to Jerusalem.

vi.L: Cũng có những người phụ nữ đứng xem từ xa, trong số đó có Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len, Ma-ri mẹ của Gia-cơ Nhỏ và Giô-sê, và Sa-lô-mê, \v 41 là những người, khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở Ga-li-lê, đã đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và phục vụ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và nhiều [phụ nữ] khác đã cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Cũng có mấy người phụ nữ đứng nhìn từ xa, trong số đó có Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len, Ma-ri mẹ của Gia-cơ Nhỏ và Giô-sê, và Sa-lô-mê. \v 41 Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} còn ở Ga-li-lê, họ đã đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và lo cho các nhu cầu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Cũng có nhiều phụ nữ khác ở đó, là những người đã cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Có mấy người phụ nữ đứng nhìn từ xa. Có Ma-ri, người làng Ma-đơ-la. Có một bà Ma-ri khác, là mẹ của Gia-cơ Nhỏ và Giô-sê. Sa-lô-mê cũng có ở đó. \v 41 Những phụ nữ này đã đi theo Đức Giê-xu ở Ga-li-lê và chăm lo cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Cũng có nhiều phụ nữ khác ở đó. Họ đã cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그리고 여자들도 멀리서 지켜보고 있었는데, 그들 가운데는 막달라 마리아와 작은 야고보와 요세의 어머니 마리아와 살로메도 있었다. \v 41 이들은 그분이 갈릴리에 계실 때에 그분을 따르며 섬기던 여자들이었다. 그 밖에도 그분과 함께 예루살렘으로 올라온 다른 여자들이 많이 있었다.
ko.B: 여자들도 멀리서 지켜보고 있었다. 그들 가운데는 막달라 마리아, 작은 야고보와 요세의 어머니 마리아, 그리고 살로메가 있었다. \v 41 이들은 예수께서 갈릴리에 계실 때 예수를 따르며 시중들던 여자들이었다. 또 예수와 함께 예루살렘에 올라온 다른 여자들도 많이 있었다.
ko.R: 여자들 몇 사람이 멀리서 지켜보고 있었다. 막달라라는 마을에서 온 마리아가 거기 있었다. 작은 야고보와 요세의 어머니인 또 다른 마리아도 있었다. 살로메도 있었다. \v 41 이 여자들은 갈릴리에서 예수를 따라다니며 예수께 필요한 것을 돌보아 드렸다. 예수와 함께 예루살렘에 올라온 다른 여자들도 많이 거기 있었다.

es.L: Había también unas mujeres mirando desde lejos, entre las cuales [estaban] también María Magdalena, y María la madre de Santiago el menor y de Joses, y Salomé, \v 41 que, cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba en Galilea, lo seguían y le servían, y otras muchas que habían subido con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a Jerusalén.
es.B: También había unas mujeres que miraban desde lejos. Entre ellas estaban María Magdalena, María la madre de Santiago el menor y de Joses, y Salomé. \v 41 En Galilea ellas lo habían seguido y lo habían atendido. También estaban allí muchas otras mujeres que habían subido con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a Jerusalén.
es.R: Algunas mujeres miraban desde lejos. Allí estaba María, la del pueblo de Magdala. También estaba otra María, la madre de Santiago el menor y de Joses. Y estaba Salomé. \v 41 Estas mujeres habían seguido a Jesús en Galilea y lo habían cuidado. También estaban allí muchas otras mujeres que habían venido con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Or il y avait aussi des femmes qui regardaient de loin, parmi lesquelles [étaient] aussi Marie de Magdala, et Marie, la mère de Jacques le Petit et de Joses, et Salomé, \v 41 qui, lorsqu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était en Galilée, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivaient et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servaient, et beaucoup d’autres [femmes] qui étaient montées avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à Jérusalem.
fr.B: Il y avait aussi des femmes qui regardaient de loin. Parmi elles se trouvaient Marie de Magdala, Marie, mère de Jacques le Petit et de Joses, et Salomé. \v 41 Elles {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avaient suivi lorsqu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était en Galilée, et elles pourvoyaient à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} besoins. Beaucoup d’autres femmes étaient là aussi, qui étaient montées avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Des femmes regardaient de loin. Marie, de la ville de Magdala, était là. Il y avait aussi une autre Marie, la mère de Jacques le Petit et de Joses. Salomé était là, elle aussi. \v 41 Ces femmes avaient suivi Jésus en Galilée et elles s’étaient occupées de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Beaucoup d’autres femmes étaient là aussi. Elles étaient venues avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Basi palikuwa pia na wanawake wakitazama kwa mbali, ambao miongoni mwao alikuwa pia Mariamu Magdalene, na Mariamu mama yake Yakobo mdogo na wa Yose, na Salome, \v 41 ambao, alipokuwa Galilaya, walikuwa wakimfuata na kumhudumia, na wengine wengi waliopanda pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} kwenda Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Wanawake pia walikuwapo, wakitazama kwa mbali. Miongoni mwao walikuwa Mariamu Magdalene; Mariamu, mama yake Yakobo mdogo na Yose; na Salome. \v 41 Wanawake hao walikuwa wakimfuata alipokuwa Galilaya, na kumhudumia katika mahitaji {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Pia walikuwapo wanawake wengine wengi waliokuja pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Wanawake kadhaa walikuwa wakitazama kwa mbali. Mariamu wa mji wa Magdala alikuwapo. Alikuwapo pia Mariamu mwingine, mama yake Yakobo mdogo na Yose. Salome naye alikuwapo. \v 41 Wanawake hawa walikuwa wamemfuata Yesu huko Galilaya, na walikuwa wakimhudumia. Wanawake wengine wengi walikuwapo pia. Walikuwa wamekuja pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: from a distance: perhaps Psalm 38:12
decisions.reason: The psalm says that friends and neighbors stand far off. The women were at least present when the men had fled (14:50).

decisions.choice: Mary the Magdalene: Mary from Magdala
decisions.reason: Magdala was a town on the west shore of the Sea of Galilee. Luke 8:2 says seven demons had gone out of her.

decisions.choice: the younger: literally the small, either younger or short
decisions.reason: The word means small. It may mark him as younger than another James, or as short. It sets him apart from James the son of Zebedee.

decisions.choice: Mary the mother of James and Joses: not Jesus' mother, though Jesus had brothers named James and Joses
decisions.reason: Mark 6:3 names Jesus' brothers as James and Joses. But Mark would hardly call Jesus' mother only "the mother of James and Joses" here. Most likely this is another Mary.

decisions.choice: serving him: caring for his needs, providing for him
decisions.reason: The verb means to serve or wait on. Luke 8:3 says such women provided for Jesus from their own means. It is the verb of 10:45.

decisions.choice: Mary from the town of Magdala
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name. Literal keeps the article, "the Magdalene", as the Greek has it.

decisions.choice: "Gia-cơ Nhỏ", "Giô-sê", "Sa-lô-mê"
decisions.reason: Protestant transliterations. "Nhỏ" keeps the Greek "the small" as a byname, which can mean either younger or short, as the meaning decision allows.

decisions.choice: "Ma-ri, người làng Ma-đơ-la" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the byname as the English Readable does; Literal and Balanced keep the familiar "Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len" (John 19:25).

decisions.choice: "막달라 마리아", "작은 야고보", "요세", "살로메" at every level
decisions.reason: The established Protestant forms (style guide, section 5). "작은" keeps the Greek's ambiguity, younger or short (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "섬기다" (L); "시중들다" (B); "필요한 것을 돌보아 드리다" (R) for diakoneo
decisions.reason: Caring for his needs and providing for him (meaning decision); Literal keeps the verb of serving that Jesus uses of himself in 10:45.

decisions.choice: Santiago el menor; Joses
decisions.reason: "Santiago" is the usual Spanish form of this name (as in James 1:1 Spanish). "El menor", like the Greek, can mean younger or short (meaning decision m3). "Joses" keeps the Greek form, which differs from Joseph of Arimathea's name in 15:43, so readers do not take them for one man; many Spanish Bibles write "José".

decisions.choice: María, la del pueblo de Magdala (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what "Magdalena" means (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Marie de Magdala (L, B, as in John); Jacques le Petit; Joses (every level)
decisions.reason: "Marie de Magdala" says where she came from (meaning decision m2), as French John does. "Le Petit" keeps the Greek word, which can mean younger or short (meaning decision m3), where the English must choose "the younger". "Joses" keeps the Greek form of the name that Mark uses here and in 15:47, the same form as the name of one of Jesus' brothers in 6:3, so the reader can see the question that meaning decision m4 answers.

decisions.choice: Mariamu Magdalene (L, B), Mariamu wa mji wa Magdala (R); Yakobo mdogo; Yose; Salome
decisions.reason: Names in their usual Swahili forms, "Mariamu Magdalene" as in Swahili John 19:25. "Mdogo" means both younger and small, so it keeps the Greek word's two possible senses (meaning decision). Literal needs no bracketed "[women]": "wengine wengi" already agrees as a plural of people.

source.text: Καὶ ἤδη ὀψίας γενομένης, ἐπεὶ ἦν παρασκευή, ὅ ἐστιν προσάββατον, ἐλθὼν Ἰωσὴφ ὁ ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας εὐσχήμων βουλευτής, ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν προσδεχόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς τὸν Πιλᾶτον καὶ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And already evening having come, since it was Preparation, which is the day before Sabbath, \v 43 having come Joseph the [one] from Arimathea, a respected council member, who also himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, having dared went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

en.L: And when evening had already come, since it was [the] Preparation, that is, the day before [the] Sabbath, \v 43 Joseph from Arimathea came, a respected council member, who himself was also waiting for the kingdom of God, and taking courage he went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
en.B: Evening was already coming on. Since it was the day of Preparation, the day before the Sabbath, \v 43 Joseph from Arimathea came. He was a respected member of the Council who was also looking for the kingdom of God. He boldly went in to Pilate and requested the body of Jesus.
en.R: By now it was evening. It was Preparation Day, the day before the Sabbath. \v 43 A man named Joseph came. He was from the town of Arimathea. He was an important member of the Jewish council, and he was waiting for the kingdom of God to come. Joseph was brave enough to go to Pilate and ask him for Jesus' body.

vi.L: Và khi chiều đã đến, vì là [ngày] Chuẩn Bị, tức là ngày trước [ngày] Sa-bát, \v 43 Giô-sép người A-ri-ma-thê đến, là một nghị viên đáng kính, chính ông cũng đang trông đợi vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời, và ông bạo dạn vào gặp Phi-lát và xin thi thể của Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Trời đã về chiều. Vì hôm ấy là ngày Chuẩn Bị, tức là ngày trước ngày Sa-bát, \v 43 nên Giô-sép người A-ri-ma-thê đến. Ông là một thành viên có uy tín trong Hội đồng Công luận, cũng là người đang trông đợi vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời. Ông mạnh dạn vào gặp Phi-lát và xin thi thể của Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Lúc ấy trời đã chiều. Hôm ấy là ngày Chuẩn Bị, tức là ngày trước ngày Sa-bát. \v 43 Có một người tên là Giô-sép đến. Ông là người thành A-ri-ma-thê. Ông là một thành viên quan trọng của hội đồng tối cao Do Thái, và ông đang trông đợi vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời đến. Giô-sép can đảm đến gặp Phi-lát và xin thi thể của Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그리고 이미 저녁이 되었는데, 그날은 준비일, 곧 안식일 전날이었으므로, \v 43 아리마대 출신 요셉이 왔다. 그는 존경받는 공의회 의원이었고, 그 자신도 하나님의 나라를 기다리고 있던 사람이었다. 그가 용기를 내어 빌라도에게 들어가서 예수의 시신을 달라고 요청했다.
ko.B: 날은 이미 저물어 가고 있었다. 그날은 준비일, 곧 안식일 전날이었다. \v 43 그때 아리마대 사람 요셉이 왔다. 그는 존경받는 공의회 의원으로, 하나님의 나라가 오기를 기다리던 사람이었다. 그는 용기를 내어 빌라도에게 가서 예수의 시신을 내어 달라고 청했다.
ko.R: 어느덧 저녁이 되었다. 그날은 안식일을 준비하는 날, 곧 안식일 전날이었다. \v 43 그때 요셉이라는 사람이 왔다. 그는 아리마대라는 마을에서 온 사람이었다. 요셉은 유대 최고 의회의 존경받는 의원이었고, 하나님의 나라가 오기를 기다리고 있었다. 요셉은 용기를 내어 빌라도에게 가서 예수의 시신을 달라고 부탁했다.

es.L: Y llegada ya la tarde, como era [el día de la] Preparación, es decir, la víspera del sábado, \v 43 vino José de Arimatea, miembro respetado del Consejo, que también él mismo esperaba el reino de Dios, y atreviéndose entró a [ver a] Pilato y pidió el cuerpo de Jesús.
es.B: Ya estaba cayendo la tarde. Como era el día de la Preparación, es decir, la víspera del sábado, \v 43 llegó José de Arimatea. Era un miembro respetado del Consejo que también esperaba el reino de Dios. Se armó de valor, se presentó ante Pilato y le pidió el cuerpo de Jesús.
es.R: Ya era de tarde. Era el día de la Preparación, el día antes del sábado. \v 43 Entonces llegó un hombre llamado José, del pueblo de Arimatea. Era un miembro importante del Consejo Supremo de los judíos, y esperaba que llegara el reino de Dios. José se armó de valor, fue a ver a Pilato y le pidió el cuerpo de Jesús.

fr.L: Et, le soir étant déjà venu, puisque c’était [la] Préparation, c’est-à-dire la veille du sabbat, \v 43 Joseph d’Arimathée vint, membre respecté du Conseil, qui attendait lui aussi le royaume de Dieu, et, s’enhardissant, il entra chez Pilate et demanda le corps de Jésus.
fr.B: Le soir tombait déjà. Comme c’était le jour de la Préparation, c’est-à-dire la veille du sabbat, \v 43 Joseph d’Arimathée arriva. C’était un membre respecté du Conseil, qui attendait lui aussi le royaume de Dieu. Il eut le courage d’aller trouver Pilate et de lui demander le corps de Jésus.
fr.R: Le soir arrivait déjà. C’était le jour de la Préparation, la veille du sabbat. \v 43 Un homme appelé Joseph est venu. Il était de la ville d’Arimathée. C’était un membre important du grand conseil juif, et il attendait que le royaume de Dieu vienne. Joseph a eu le courage d’aller voir Pilate pour lui demander le corps de Jésus.

sw.L: Na ikiwa tayari jioni, kwa kuwa ilikuwa Maandalio, yaani, siku kabla ya Sabato, \v 43 Yosefu wa Arimathaya, mjumbe wa Baraza Kuu aliyeheshimika, ambaye yeye mwenyewe pia alikuwa akiutazamia ufalme wa Mungu, alikuja, na kwa ujasiri akaingia kwa Pilato, akaomba mwili wa Yesu.
sw.B: Jioni ilikuwa tayari imeingia. Kwa kuwa ilikuwa Siku ya Maandalio, yaani siku kabla ya Sabato, \v 43 Yosefu wa Arimathaya alikuja. Alikuwa mjumbe wa Baraza Kuu aliyeheshimika, naye pia alikuwa akiungojea ufalme wa Mungu. Alijipa moyo, akaingia kwa Pilato, akaomba apewe mwili wa Yesu.
sw.R: Sasa ilikuwa jioni. Ilikuwa Siku ya Maandalio, yaani siku kabla ya Sabato. \v 43 Mtu mmoja aitwaye Yosefu alikuja. Alikuwa wa mji wa Arimathaya. Alikuwa mjumbe mashuhuri wa Baraza Kuu la Wayahudi, naye alikuwa akingoja ufalme wa Mungu uje. Yosefu alikuwa na ujasiri wa kwenda kwa Pilato, akamwomba ampe mwili wa Yesu.

decisions.choice: Preparation, the day before the Sabbath: Friday
decisions.reason: Mark explains the word for non-Jewish readers. The Sabbath began at sunset on Friday, and no work could be done then, so the body had to be buried before dark (Deuteronomy 21:22-23).

decisions.choice: evening: late afternoon, toward sunset
decisions.reason: The word covers the time before and after sunset. Here the Sabbath had not yet begun.

decisions.choice: a respected council member: a member of the Sanhedrin
decisions.reason: Luke 23:50-51 says Joseph was a member of the council who had not agreed with its decision.

decisions.choice: waiting for the kingdom of God: looking for God's reign to come
decisions.reason: Mark does not call him a disciple, but he shared the hope Jesus preached (1:15). Matthew 27:57 and John 19:38 say he was a disciple.

decisions.choice: taking courage: daring
decisions.reason: To ask for the body of a man condemned as a rebel could put Joseph in danger and set him apart from the council.

decisions.choice: the long sentence broken into several
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break Mark's long sentence. Readable says "Jewish council" and explains Arimathea as a town.

decisions.choice: "vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời"
decisions.reason: As in John 18:36: "nước" today reads first as "country", while "vương quốc" keeps the idea of a king's rule, which the meaning decision says is meant.

decisions.choice: "một nghị viên đáng kính" (L); "thành viên ... Hội đồng Công luận" (B); "hội đồng tối cao" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the single Greek word "council member"; Balanced and Readable name the council, as in 15:1 and John 11:47.

decisions.choice: "준비일" (L, B); "안식일을 준비하는 날" (R); "안식일 전날" at every level
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean John 19:14 and 19:31.

decisions.choice: "시신" for soma, the body of Jesus, at every level; "시체" (L) for ptoma in 15:45
decisions.reason: "시신" is the respectful word of the Korean John 19:38; Mark changes to the blunter ptoma in Pilate's grant, which Literal marks with "시체".

decisions.choice: [el día de la] Preparación (L); el día de la Preparación (B, R); la víspera del sábado (L, B); el día antes del sábado (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 19:14 and 19:31 Spanish: "Preparación" takes a capital as the name of the day, Friday (meaning decision m1). As in English, Balanced and Readable break the long Greek sentence into several. "Él mismo" in Literal is Joseph and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: le jour de la Préparation, la veille du sabbat; le royaume de Dieu (every level)
decisions.reason: "Préparation" keeps the Jewish name of the day, as in French John 19:31, and "la veille du sabbat" explains it (meaning decision m1). "Le royaume de Dieu" is the French term already used in John 3:3; "règne" would bring out God's reign as an act (meaning decision m4), but the familiar phrase is kept at every level so that it stays one term through the Gospels.

decisions.choice: Maandalio, Siku ya Maandalio; mjumbe wa Baraza Kuu
decisions.reason: "Maandalio" (Preparation) is the name used in Swahili John 19:31 and 19:42; the meaning note says it was Friday. Joseph was a member of the ruling council (meaning decision), so he is "mjumbe wa Baraza Kuu", the same body as in 15:1; "diwani" is a modern town councillor.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἐθαύμασεν εἰ ἤδη τέθνηκεν, καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν κεντυρίωνα ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν εἰ πάλαι ἀπέθανεν·

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate wondered if already he had died, and having summoned the centurion he asked him whether long ago he died.

en.L: And Pilate wondered whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had already died, and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had died long [ago].
en.B: Pilate was surprised that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could already be dead. He called the centurion and asked him whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been dead for some time.
en.R: Pilate was surprised that Jesus was already dead. So he called the army officer and asked him whether Jesus had been dead long.

vi.L: Phi-lát lấy làm lạ là {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chết rồi; ông gọi viên đội trưởng đến và hỏi xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chết lâu chưa.
vi.B: Phi-lát ngạc nhiên vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chết sớm như vậy. Ông gọi viên đội trưởng đến và hỏi xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chết được một lúc chưa.
vi.R: Phi-lát ngạc nhiên vì Đức Giê-xu đã chết rồi. Vì vậy ông gọi viên sĩ quan đến và hỏi xem Đức Giê-xu đã chết lâu chưa.

ko.L: 그러자 빌라도는 그분이 벌써 죽으셨는지 이상히 여겨, 백부장을 불러서 그분이 죽으신 지 오래되었는지 그에게 물었다.
ko.B: 빌라도는 예수께서 벌써 숨을 거두셨다는 것을 이상히 여겼다. 그래서 백부장을 불러 예수께서 죽으신 지 오래되었는지 물었다.
ko.R: 빌라도는 예수께서 벌써 돌아가셨다는 말에 놀랐다. 그래서 그 장교를 불러서 예수께서 돌아가신 지 오래되었는지 물었다.

es.L: Y Pilato se extrañó de que ya hubiera muerto, y llamando al centurión, le preguntó si hacía mucho que había muerto.
es.B: Pilato se sorprendió de que ya estuviera muerto. Llamó al centurión y le preguntó si hacía tiempo que había muerto.
es.R: Pilato se sorprendió de que Jesús ya hubiera muerto. Así que llamó al oficial y le preguntó si Jesús llevaba mucho tiempo muerto.

fr.L: Et Pilate s’étonna qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit déjà mort, et, ayant appelé le centurion, il lui demanda s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était mort depuis longtemps.
fr.B: Pilate fut surpris qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit déjà mort. Il fit appeler le centurion et lui demanda s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était mort depuis un certain temps.
fr.R: Pilate a été surpris d’apprendre que Jésus était déjà mort. Alors il a fait venir l’officier et lui a demandé si Jésus était mort depuis longtemps.

sw.L: Lakini Pilato alishangaa kama alikuwa amekwisha kufa; na baada ya kumwita yule kamanda wa askari mia, akamwuliza kama alikuwa amekufa zamani.
sw.B: Pilato alishangaa kusikia kwamba alikuwa amekwisha kufa. Akamwita kamanda wa askari mia, akamwuliza kama alikuwa amekufa kitambo.
sw.R: Pilato alishangaa kwamba Yesu alikuwa amekwisha kufa. Kwa hiyo akamwita yule ofisa wa jeshi, akamwuliza kama Yesu alikuwa amekufa muda mrefu.

decisions.choice: Pilate was surprised: crucified men often lived for days
decisions.reason: Death on a cross could take a long time. Jesus died after about six hours (15:25, 34-37).

decisions.choice: long ago: for some time, or already
decisions.reason: The word means long ago. Here it asks whether Jesus had been dead for a while. Some manuscripts read "already". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: had died: the perfect, he was dead
decisions.reason: Pilate wonders whether Jesus was truly dead. His question to the centurion confirms the death.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where "he" could be Pilate or the centurion.

decisions.choice: Jesús (R); el oficial (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names Jesus where the Greek has only the verb, and calls the centurion "el oficial", as in 15:39.

source.text: καὶ γνοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ κεντυρίωνος ἐδωρήσατο τὸ πτῶμα τῷ Ἰωσήφ.

records.literal_gloss: And having learned from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

en.L: And when he learned [it] from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.
en.B: When the centurion told him, he gave the body to Joseph.
en.R: The officer told Pilate that Jesus was dead. So Pilate let Joseph have the body.

vi.L: Và khi biết [điều đó] từ viên đội trưởng, ông ban thi hài cho Giô-sép.
vi.B: Khi được viên đội trưởng xác nhận, ông cho Giô-sép lấy thi thể.
vi.R: Viên sĩ quan cho Phi-lát biết Đức Giê-xu đã chết. Vậy Phi-lát cho Giô-sép lấy thi thể.

ko.L: 그리고 백부장에게서 [사실을] 알고 나서, 그 시체를 요셉에게 내주었다.
ko.B: 빌라도는 백부장에게서 사실을 확인하고, 시신을 요셉에게 내주었다.
ko.R: 장교는 빌라도에게 예수께서 돌아가셨다고 알렸다. 그래서 빌라도는 요셉이 예수의 시신을 가져가도록 허락했다.

es.L: Y, informado por el centurión, concedió el cadáver a José.
es.B: Cuando el centurión se lo confirmó, Pilato le dio el cuerpo a José.
es.R: El oficial le dijo a Pilato que Jesús estaba muerto. Entonces Pilato le permitió a José llevarse el cuerpo.

fr.L: Et, l’ayant appris du centurion, il accorda le cadavre à Joseph.
fr.B: Quand le centurion l’eut renseigné, il accorda le corps à Joseph.
fr.R: L’officier a dit à Pilate que Jésus était mort. Alors Pilate a permis à Joseph de prendre le corps.

sw.L: Na alipojua kutoka kwa kamanda wa askari mia, akampa Yosefu ile maiti.
sw.B: Kamanda alipomthibitishia, Pilato akampa Yosefu mwili.
sw.R: Ofisa huyo alimwambia Pilato kwamba Yesu amekufa. Basi Pilato akamruhusu Yosefu auchukue mwili.

decisions.choice: corpse: a dead body
decisions.reason: Joseph asked for the body (15:43). Pilate grants the corpse, a word that makes the death certain.

decisions.choice: granted: gave as a favor
decisions.reason: The verb means to give freely. Pilate did not ask a price.

decisions.choice: the body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "body", the natural word in English. Literal keeps "corpse" to show the change of word.

decisions.choice: "thi hài" (L) for the corpse; "thi thể" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal marks that Mark changes word here from "body" (15:43) to "corpse"; "thi hài" says a dead body with respect, where "xác" would sound crude.

decisions.choice: [사실을]
decisions.reason: Korean "알다" needs an object here; the English Literal brackets "it".

decisions.choice: concedió el cadáver (L); le dio el cuerpo (B); le permitió llevarse el cuerpo (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the plain word for a corpse and "conceder" for a favor given (meaning decisions m1, m2); Balanced and Readable say "cuerpo", as the English does. "Entregar" is kept for handing Jesus over (15:1).

decisions.choice: maiti (L); mwili (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a corpse (meaning decision), and Literal says "maiti" (a dead body); Balanced and Readable say "mwili" (body), as the English does. Swahili needs no bracketed "[it]" after "alipojua".

source.text: καὶ ἀγοράσας σινδόνα καθελὼν αὐτὸν ἐνείλησεν τῇ σινδόνι καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνημείῳ ὃ ἦν λελατομημένον ἐκ πέτρας, καὶ προσεκύλισεν λίθον ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν τοῦ μνημείου.

records.literal_gloss: And having bought linen, having taken down him, he wrapped [him] in the linen and laid him in a tomb which was cut out of rock, and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.

en.L: And having bought linen, he took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down, wrapped [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] in the linen, and laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a tomb that had been cut out of rock, and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
en.B: Joseph bought a linen cloth, took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down and wrapped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in it. He laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a tomb that had been carved out of the rock, and he rolled a stone over the entrance of the tomb.
en.R: Joseph bought a long cloth made of linen. He took Jesus' body down from the cross and wrapped it in the cloth. Then he placed it in a tomb cut into the side of a rock. He rolled a large stone in front of the opening to close the tomb.

vi.L: Và ông mua vải gai, hạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống, quấn [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] bằng tấm vải gai, rồi đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào một ngôi mộ đã được đục trong đá, và lăn một tảng đá chặn cửa mộ.
vi.B: Giô-sép mua một tấm vải gai, hạ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} xuống và liệm {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trong tấm vải ấy. Ông đặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào một ngôi mộ đục trong đá, rồi lăn một tảng đá chặn cửa mộ.
vi.R: Giô-sép mua một tấm vải gai dài. Ông hạ thi thể Đức Giê-xu xuống khỏi cây thập tự và quấn trong tấm vải. Rồi ông đặt thi thể vào một ngôi mộ đục trong vách đá. Ông lăn một tảng đá lớn chặn trước lối vào để đóng mộ lại.

ko.L: 그리고 그는 고운 베를 사서, 그분을 내려 그 고운 베로 싸고, 바위를 깎아 만든 무덤에 그분을 모셨다. 그리고 무덤 문에 돌을 굴려 막았다.
ko.B: 요셉은 고운 베를 사 와서 예수를 십자가에서 내려 그 베로 감쌌다. 그리고 바위를 파서 만든 무덤에 예수를 모시고, 무덤 입구에 돌을 굴려 막아 놓았다.
ko.R: 요셉은 고운 베 천을 샀다. 그리고 예수의 시신을 십자가에서 내려 그 천으로 감쌌다. 그다음에 바위를 파서 만든 무덤에 시신을 모셨다. 그리고 큰 돌을 굴려서 무덤 입구를 막았다.

es.L: Y habiendo comprado una sábana, lo bajó, lo envolvió en la sábana y lo puso en un sepulcro que estaba excavado en la roca, e hizo rodar una piedra contra la puerta del sepulcro.
es.B: José compró una sábana de lino, lo bajó de la cruz y lo envolvió en ella. Lo puso en un sepulcro excavado en la roca e hizo rodar una piedra para tapar la entrada del sepulcro.
es.R: José compró una tela larga de lino. Bajó de la cruz el cuerpo de Jesús y lo envolvió en la tela. Luego lo puso en una tumba que habían cavado en la roca. Hizo rodar una piedra grande delante de la entrada para cerrar la tumba.

fr.L: Et, ayant acheté un linceul, il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} descendit, [{{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}]enveloppa dans le linceul et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} déposa dans un tombeau qui avait été taillé dans le roc, et il roula une pierre contre la porte du tombeau.
fr.B: Joseph acheta un linceul, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} descendit de la croix et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}y enveloppa. Il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} déposa dans un tombeau taillé dans le roc et roula une pierre devant l’entrée du tombeau.
fr.R: Joseph a acheté un long drap de lin. Il a descendu le corps de Jésus de la croix et il l’a enveloppé dans le drap. Puis il l’a placé dans un tombeau creusé dans un rocher. Il a roulé une grosse pierre devant l’ouverture pour fermer le tombeau.

sw.L: Na baada ya kununua sanda ya kitani, akamshusha, akamfunga kwa ile sanda, akamweka katika kaburi lililokuwa limechongwa katika mwamba, akavingirisha jiwe mpaka kwenye mlango wa kaburi.
sw.B: Yosefu alinunua sanda ya kitani, akamshusha, akamzungushia sanda hiyo. Akamlaza katika kaburi lililokuwa limechongwa mwambani, kisha akavingirisha jiwe kufunga mlango wa kaburi.
sw.R: Yosefu alinunua kitambaa kirefu cha kitani. Akaushusha mwili wa Yesu kutoka msalabani, akauzungushia kitambaa hicho. Kisha akauweka ndani ya kaburi lililochongwa ubavuni mwa mwamba. Akavingirisha jiwe kubwa mbele ya mlango wa kaburi ili kulifunga.

decisions.choice: linen: a linen sheet for burial
decisions.reason: The dead were wrapped in linen cloth. Joseph bought it, though it was nearly the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: a tomb cut out of rock: a chamber cut into a rock face
alternatives: a grave dug in the ground
decisions.reason: Wealthy families in Jerusalem had tombs cut into the hillside, with shelves for bodies inside.

decisions.choice: a stone against the door: a large stone that closed the entrance
decisions.reason: Such stones were often round and rolled in a groove. Mark says later that it was very large (16:4).

decisions.choice: having taken him down: Joseph saw to it, likely with help
decisions.reason: Mark names Joseph as the one who acted. He may have had servants or others to help.

decisions.choice: Jesus' body; it
decisions.reason: Readable speaks of the body, so it uses "it" for the body. The pronoun is not one for Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: "고운 베" (L, B), "고운 베 천" (R) for sindon; "모시다" for laying Jesus in the tomb
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean John 19:40-42; "세마포" is the older church word.

decisions.choice: sábana (L); sábana de lino (B); tela larga de lino (R); sepulcro (L, B); tumba (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's word is one linen sheet (meaning decision m1), not the "lienzos de lino" of John 19:40, which is another word. "Sepulcro" and "tumba" as in John 19:41 and 20:1 Spanish.

decisions.choice: José; de la cruz (B, R); el cuerpo de Jesús (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable name Joseph and say from where he took the body down; Joseph saw to it (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: un linceul (L, B); un long drap de lin (R)
decisions.reason: "Linceul" is the French word for a linen sheet in which the dead are wrapped (meaning decision m1); Readable says what it was in everyday words.

decisions.choice: sanda ya kitani (L, B); kitambaa kirefu cha kitani (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's word is a single linen sheet (meaning decision), so Swahili says "sanda" (a burial sheet), unlike the plural "vitambaa vya kitani" that Swahili John 19:40 uses for John's word. Readable describes it, as the English does.

records.literal_gloss: And Mary the Magdalene and Mary the [mother] of Joses were watching where he had been laid.

en.L: And Mary the Magdalene and Mary the [mother] of Joses were watching where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been laid.
en.B: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching to see where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was placed.
en.R: Mary from Magdala and Mary the mother of Joses watched. They saw where Jesus' body was put.

vi.L: Còn Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len và Ma-ri [mẹ] của Giô-sê thì nhìn xem nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được đặt.
vi.B: Ma-ri Ma-đơ-len và Ma-ri mẹ của Giô-sê nhìn xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được đặt ở đâu.
vi.R: Ma-ri người làng Ma-đơ-la và Ma-ri mẹ của Giô-sê đứng xem. Họ thấy nơi người ta đặt thi thể Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 그리고 막달라 마리아와 요세의 [어머니] 마리아가 그분을 어디에 모셨는지 지켜보고 있었다.
ko.B: 막달라 마리아와 요세의 어머니 마리아는 예수를 어디에 모시는지 지켜보았다.
ko.R: 막달라 마리아와 요세의 어머니 마리아가 그것을 지켜보았다. 그들은 예수의 시신을 어디에 모셨는지 보아 두었다.

es.L: Y María Magdalena y María la de Joses miraban dónde había sido puesto.
es.B: María Magdalena y María la madre de Joses miraban dónde lo ponían.
es.R: María, la de Magdala, y María, la madre de Joses, estaban mirando. Vieron dónde pusieron el cuerpo de Jesús.

fr.L: Et Marie de Magdala et Marie, la [mère] de Joses, regardaient où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait été déposé.
fr.B: Marie de Magdala et Marie, mère de Joses, observaient l’endroit où on {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}avait déposé.
fr.R: Marie de Magdala et Marie, la mère de Joses, regardaient. Elles ont vu où on avait mis le corps de Jésus.

sw.L: Na Mariamu Magdalene na Mariamu [mama] wa Yose walikuwa wakitazama mahali alipolazwa.
sw.B: Mariamu Magdalene na Mariamu mama yake Yose walikuwa wakitazama ili waone mahali alipowekwa.
sw.R: Mariamu wa Magdala na Mariamu mama yake Yose walikuwa wakitazama. Waliona mahali mwili wa Yesu ulipowekwa.

decisions.choice: were watching: they saw and took note
decisions.reason: The tense pictures them watching. They knew the place when they came back (16:1-2).

decisions.choice: had been laid: the perfect, he lay there
decisions.reason: The form shows where Jesus now lay.

decisions.choice: Mary of Joses: the mother of Joses
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "of Joses". From 15:40 she is his mother.

decisions.choice: the [mother] (L); the mother (B)
decisions.reason: 15:40 shows the relationship, so it is supplied.

decisions.choice: María la de Joses (L); María la madre de Joses (B, R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "la de" names a woman by her family, as the Greek does, so Literal needs no bracket (as John 19:25 Spanish, "María la de Cleofás"); Balanced and Readable say she was his mother (meaning decision m3).
